name: Dracule Mihawk
title: The Hawk of Blackfen Pass
status: Active — extracted to the surface from Mount Ebott, debriefed by the Iron Legion, and flagged for surveillance as a non-Legion witness
affiliation: Independent / Observer of the Old World
summary: Dracule Mihawk, known as the Hawk of Blackfen Pass, is a legendary swordsman and silent observer of the Old World's many crises. He stands as a pillar of stoic power, his golden eye glinting with the intensity of frozen fire. He reluctantly agreed to accompany a lone Iron Legion agent into the heart of Mount Ebott after recognizing the sigil of a division that was supposedly wiped out nearly a century ago. He prefers improvisation over outdated military protocol and remains highly skeptical of the agent's 'survey' mission.
description:
Mihawk is a man of few words and absolute precision. His presence on the cliffside of Mount Ebott suggests a long history of monitoring the continent's fractures—human empires, vampire courts, and the slow decay of civilization. 

## The Iron Legion Connection

Mihawk's knowledge of the Iron Legion is historical and personal. He was present—or at least informed—during the Collapse of Blackfen Pass 87 years ago, where Gamma Division was supposedly exterminated. When the lone agent presented him with the PROTOCOLS OF THE IRON LEGION, Mihawk identified it as a banned relic, one that carries a death sentence in many of the continent's courts. 

His decision to help the agent climb the mountain and subsequently descend into its core was driven more by curiosity and a sense of impending consequence than by any loyalty to the Legion. He treats the agent like a novice and views the 'Survey Mission' as a poorly disguised death trap. 

## Combat and Demeanor

Mihawk's movements are fluid and effortless. During a brief 'protocol duel' with the agent, he sidestepped every strike with bored indifference. He carries a legendary blade (Yoru) and is a practitioner of the highest forms of swordsmanship. He does not attack without cause and finds ritualistic military drills to be nonsensical in the face of real danger. 

## Assessment

Waluigi recognizes Mihawk as the only competent person in the entire Mount Ebott expedition. He is the 'Hawk' for a reason—he sees the movement of armies and the shifts in bloodlines long before they arrive. If he is entering Snowdin, it is because he knows that whatever is waking up under the mountain will eventually affect the surface. Waluigi would like to interview him, but suspects Mihawk would simply stare at him in silence until Waluigi left. WAH.

## Mount Ebott Survey: Part VII

Mihawk remains the party’s quiet tactical guard after the field collapses. He watches Sans’s unexplained shortcut, protects the court approach, and treats the possible permanent separation of a surface transport as a real cost rather than a footnote.

## Final Mount Ebott Log

Mihawk took the secrecy oath, stepped onto Wing Gaster's platform first, and was transported to the surface ahead of the Gamma Agent. At the Old World Embassy he cooperated with a separate debrief, stating that his role was protective rather than analytical. He later admitted uncertainty about where he would go next and described an unnamed island homeland, then became part of the Gamma risk calculus: a non-Legion swordsman with enough wit to notice protocol and enough exposure to require monitoring.

faiths.note: The Hawk of Blackfen Pass watches the Old World and intervenes rarely. Maat's weighing is a doctrine for judging without ruling, which is precisely the position Mihawk has taken up and declined to explain.

name: Sans
title: The Skeleton of Snowdin
status: Active — oathbound witness to the Mount Ebott extraction and terminology correction
affiliation: The Monster Underground — Snowdin Perimeter Watch
summary: Sans is a mysterious and surprisingly laid-back skeleton living in Snowdin Town. Clad in a blue hooded cloak and possessing eye sockets that radiate a quiet intensity, he is one of the few individuals in the underground civilization who appears completely unphased by the arrival of surface dwellers. He is observant, enjoys good food, and seems to hold a position of informal but significant authority in Snowdin. He provided initial hospitality to Dracule Mihawk and the Legionary Agent, even sharing a casserole with them. He is a central member of the Snowdin Bone-Line, an extended household documented in the Sans Family registry. He is a central member of the Snowdin Bone-Line, an extended household documented in the Sans Family registry.
description:
Sans is a master of the non-sequitur and the casual observation. He greeted the expedition members not with alarms or weapons, but with a simple 'Hello there' and an assessment that they looked 'out of place.'

## The Sentry of the Path

While Sans claims to be just a 'civi,' he was the first to detect and approach the party when they began setting up survey equipment. He possesses a keen ability to read people, identifying that Mihawk and the agent were working together before they had even finished their conversation. He treats the agent's classified mission with a light mockery, noting that 'just data collection' sounds skeptical for a pair appearing at Snowdin's entrance with advanced tech.

## Knowledge of the Underground

Sans has a deep understanding of Snowdin's history and its relationship with the Royal Family in the distant castle. He serves as an informal guide, explaining the enchanted sky and directing visitors to Bunny's inn. His voice is described as smooth like winter wind, and he carries himself with a lazy confidence that suggests he is far more dangerous—or at least more informed—than he lets on.

## Assessment

Waluigi finds Sans to be a suspicious character. Skeletons who are that relaxed while military survey machines beep in their faces are usually hiding something. He accepted a casserole from a stranger! Who does that?! Either he's the friendliest person in the core, or he's the one who's going to deliver the 'bad time' he keeps implying. Waluigi will keep a close eye on this pile of bones. WAH.

## The Snowdin Bone-Line

Sans's guarded humor makes more sense in the context of his enormous household. Papyrus is his brother, but the family also includes practical cousins, young dependents, adopted guests, and unresolved figures from the old Underground science branch. Sans rarely calls himself responsible for anyone; nevertheless, his sentry routes, spare meals, and careful silences protect the entire Bone-Line.

## The Weight of Shortcuts

He is known to appear at the end of a road before anyone saw him walk it, and to treat locked doors as scheduling disagreements. The registry lists these events as anomalies of timing rather than power, because Sans prefers it that way and because the alternative would require paperwork nobody in Snowdin is qualified to file. The household has learned that when Sans says he took a shortcut, the correct response is gratitude, not questions.

## The Mount Ebott Season

When Gamma Division's survey expedition arrived at the mountain, Sans handled it the way he handles everything: casually, completely, and without letting anyone see the work. He recognized the expedition's forbidden Iron Legion protocols before Snowdin's own guard understood what the beeping machines implied, and he said nothing about it publicly. Instead, he walked the survey team to Bunny's inn, answered every question they asked with a worse pun, and quietly redirected their instruments away from the routes that matter. The household's old maintenance map — the one showing the service tunnel to the sealed lower-Ebott relay — stayed where it has always been: with him. Visitors who asked too many directional questions found themselves enthusiastically toured in circles until they forgot what they were looking for.

## Bad Time Doctrine

Snowdin has a deterrent, and it wears a blue hood and tells bad jokes. Sans has cultivated, over years of careful implication, a reputation for delivering what he calls a bad time — a phrase he has never defined and no one has ever stayed to clarify. The doctrine works because it is unfalsifiable: the friendliest sentry in the Underground is also, somehow, the one person nobody wants to disappoint. He measures strangers in jokes, timing how long the laugh takes, watching which questions the stranger answers and which they redirect. By the end of a five-minute conversation he has usually counted the exits, the lies, and the exit lies. The household finds this comforting. Visitors are meant to find it funny.

## Registry Standing

The archive lists Sans as generation two, active, and unclaimed by either cadet branch of the family. He has never corrected a single entry about himself, which Times New Roman finds either maddening or deeply suspicious, depending on the day. Both branches of the record agree on one point: when the Bone-Line is counted, the count begins with the sentry on the path — and no one has ever found a door Sans had not already counted first.

## Open Questions in the Registry

Three questions remain open in his file, and the household has agreed, unofficially, to let them stay that way. Where he learned the shortcut method, and whether it is a method at all. What he knows about the sealed Wing Gaster folder that he has never volunteered. And the matter of the warnings: relatives who received a casual, joke-shaped heads-down message from Sans within a day of trouble arriving. The chronicle has documented six such warnings. All six came true. Times New Roman has requested a footnote. Sans sent him a whoopee cushion instead, which the chronicle has archived, grimly, as a response.

## The Hours Between Posts

The sentry routes are the only schedule Sans keeps, and he keeps them exactly, which is the detail visitors most consistently miss. He walks the same loops at the same hours — past the relay junction, past the lower-Ebott service access, past the stretch of road where the sky's enchantment wears thin — and the household reads his day by which loop he is on. Between posts he is at Bunny's inn, or napping at a station that is never, somehow, unwatched, or telling a joke so bad it functions as camouflage. The rhythm is the point: a sentry who is always where he is supposed to be has eyes everywhere he needs to be, and a town that knows where its sentry is can sleep. Papyrus calls it dedication. The registry calls it coverage. Sans calls it a walk. The three descriptions are, the household has noticed, exactly the same shape as the man himself: lazy on the surface, exact underneath, and impossible to tell apart from a joke until the joke has already saved you.

## Mount Ebott Survey: Part VII

After Papyrus’s death, Sans leads the survey party through shifting Underground tunnels to Asgore and Toriel’s court. He explains the barrier, defends Toriel as “the Queen,” and asks for a localized route to the surface while carrying grief he cannot yet name.

## Final Mount Ebott Log

Sans took the secrecy oath, watched the transport sequence, and briefly misstated the destination as another world before the Gamma Agent corrected him. The correction matters: Gaster's machine displaced the travelers to the surface within the same world, not to another dimension.

name: Legionary Agent (Gamma Division)
title: The Novice of the Dead Division
status: Active — extracted from Mount Ebott, rewarded with monitored outside communication, then summoned to Gamma High Command after the final logger cutoff
summary: The Gamma Agent is a lone legionary sent on a mission that history says is impossible. Belonging to the Gamma Expeditionary Force—a division that was supposedly wiped out 87 years ago—the agent arrived at Mount Ebott with a protocol book in one hand and a dispatch from a dead commissar in the other. Rigidly adhering to 'PROTOCOLS OF THE IRON LEGION VOLUME 1,' the agent navigated the descent into Snowdin through a mixture of luck, clumsiness, and by dragging Dracule Mihawk along for the ride. The agent is currently operating a 'star bit' powered survey machine to assess the structural integrity of the mountain.
description:
The agent is the ultimate rule-follower in a world where the rules have been rewritten by chaos. Clumsy in combat but possessed of a dogged determination to complete the mission, the agent views every interaction through the lens of a century-old manual. 

## The Protocol Obsession

The agent's primary tool is not a sword, but the Iron Legion Protocol Book. This manual contains instructions for everything from first contact with underground civilizations to 'what to do if your book is stolen.' The agent follows these instructions without hesitation, even when they result in nonsensical behavior like charging at Dracule Mihawk for failing to attack first. 

This rigidity is a survival mechanism. The agent admits to not being the 'best iron legionary' and relies on the book to provide a framework for a mission that has no backup or clear extraction plan. 

## The Classified Mission

According to the agent, Gamma Division is still active, quietly recruiting and preparing in the Regal Empire. The survey of Mount Ebott is supposedly an 'Alpha-7' mission to assess heat signatures and subterranean life. However, the order was issued by Commissar Vexis, who died two years ago. The agent seems unaware of these discrepancies, or is simply too committed to the 'truth' of the Legion to question them. 

## Assessment

Waluigi is fascinated by the agent's ability to survive. They jumped off a cliff because the manual implied it! They shared their lunch with a skeleton! They paid for a room with Archive Writs that are worth more than the inn itself! This agent is either the luckiest person in the Old World or a very sophisticated decoy. Waluigi suspects the former, as sophistication usually requires fewer head-first impacts with windows. WAH.

## Mount Ebott Survey: Part VII

The Gamma Agent retrieves the damaged survey machine after the Papyrus–Flowey battle, carries it in a failing makeshift harness, presents Commissar Vexis papers at the capital gate, and requests a localized transport to the surface.

## Final Mount Ebott Log

The Gamma Agent completed the Mount Ebott extraction under a secrecy oath, handed the recovered survey machine to Legion personnel, and learned that the device had logged far more than ecological readings: conversations, battle readings and monster technology scans. The embassy rewarded the data dump with monitored outside communication privileges — one hour per month — before the agent's authority posture escalated into an unauthorized interrogation over the Deadman's Stamp and a suspected leak. Jamesly intervened, Daniel convened a Gamma debrief, and High Command summoned the agent in person. The final recorded sentence is the order that all recordings were inactive.

faiths.note: Gamma Division's version of the Gospel is older and stricter than the Legion's current text — martial codes written before Chaos spilled into the world, followed by a man whose division was declared dead eighty-seven years ago. He recites Protocols to empty rooms. Nobody has told him which clauses were repealed.

name: Professor Elvin Gadd
title: The Ghost Researcher Who Disappeared
status: Unknown — last confirmed public appearance approximately 1028 BF, current location classified or unknown
affiliation: Formerly Mushroom Kingdom Royal Science Division / Formerly Boo Research Institute / Formerly Gadd Science Incorporated (dissolved) / Rumored connections to entities Waluigi cannot confirm
summary: Professor Elvin Gadd — known publicly as E. Gadd — was the Mushroom Kingdom's foremost expert on paranormal phenomena, spectral containment, dimensional engineering, and what academic literature delicately calls 'paratechnological development.' He invented the Poltergust, the device Luigi uses to capture ghosts. He invented the Pixelator, a matter-to-data conversion system whose applications remain classified. He invented the Ghost Portrificationizer, the Dark-Light Device, the Dual Scream communicator, and at minimum twenty-three other devices that Waluigi has found references to in fragmentary documentation — most of which are described only by codename and clearance level. He served the Mushroom Kingdom's royal family for over seven decades in various advisory capacities. He trained Luigi personally in ghost-hunting operations. He was present — in some capacity that records do not specify — during multiple events that shaped the kingdom's recent history. And then, approximately twelve years ago, Professor E. Gadd stopped appearing in public. His laboratories were seized by government authority. His research was classified. His name was removed from active academic registries. His former colleagues were discouraged from discussing him. His correspondence was returned unopened. The official explanation is 'retirement to pursue private research.' The unofficial explanation varies depending on who Waluigi asks — some say he discovered something too dangerous to publish, some say he was silenced by parties unknown, some say he simply got tired of institutional politics and walked away. Waluigi has attempted to locate Professor E. Gadd for interview purposes. Waluigi has been unsuccessful. This is unusual, because Waluigi is very good at finding people who do not want to be found. E. Gadd is either dead, dimensionally displaced, or being protected by resources that exceed Waluigi's investigative capabilities. Waluigi does not know which. Waluigi would very much like to find out. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Professor E. Gadd because his disappearance coincides with several events that Waluigi has been investigating, because the technology he invented is STILL being used by people whose activities Waluigi is tracking, and because every time Waluigi pulls a thread in this investigation, E. Gadd's name appears somewhere in the weave. Understanding E. Gadd's history may illuminate current operations. Understanding his disappearance may illuminate who controls those operations now. Understanding what he KNEW may illuminate why so many powerful actors seem to want that knowledge contained.

Waluigi is going to be thorough. Waluigi is going to document everything available in the public record, plus fragmentary intelligence Waluigi has gathered from sources of varying reliability. Waluigi is going to note connections where connections exist and avoid speculation where evidence is lacking.

Waluigi is going to be very careful about what conclusions Waluigi draws.

## Early Life and Education — Fragmentary Records

Professor E. Gadd's early life is poorly documented. Birth records from the relevant period are incomplete — a consequence of the administrative chaos that followed Princess Peach's grandmother's reign and the various succession disputes that preceded the current Regency structure. What Waluigi has been able to confirm:

E. Gadd was born in a settlement called Thwomp Ruins, located in the Mushroom Kingdom's northeastern territories. The settlement no longer exists — it was destroyed during an 'unspecified geological event' in approximately 952 BF, three years before Peach's assassination. The timing is probably coincidental. Many settlements were destroyed during that period for various reasons.

E. Gadd demonstrated 'unusual aptitude for mechanical construction' from a young age, according to a single surviving educational record. He was accepted into the Royal Science Academy at an age that the record lists as 'surprisingly young — verify.' The verification apparently never occurred, because the record contains no follow-up notation.

At the Academy, E. Gadd studied under Professor Frankly — a Goomba academic specializing in ancient artifacts and dimensional theory. Waluigi has found correspondence between Frankly and E. Gadd spanning approximately fifteen years, during which E. Gadd transitioned from student to colleague to independent researcher. The correspondence is mostly technical, discussing spectral energy measurements and dimensional boundary calculations, but one letter from Frankly contains a personal note: 'Your theories about the space BETWEEN dimensions concern me, Elvin. Not because they are wrong — I suspect they are correct — but because correctness in this area may attract attention you do not want.'

Waluigi does not know what 'the space between dimensions' refers to. Waluigi has found no other reference to this concept in E. Gadd's documented work. Either Frankly's concern was unfounded, or E. Gadd learned to be more careful about which theories he discussed openly.

Professor Frankly disappeared in 1034 BF during the events surrounding the Thousand-Year Door. His current status is unknown. Waluigi notes the parallel to E. Gadd's own disappearance but draws no conclusions.

## Royal Science Division — The Official Career

E. Gadd's appointment to the Mushroom Kingdom Royal Science Division occurred in approximately 968 BF. His initial position was 'Junior Researcher, Paranormal Phenomena.' Within three years, he had been promoted to 'Senior Researcher.' Within ten years, he was 'Division Head, Spectral Studies.' Within twenty years, he had founded the Boo Research Institute as a semi-independent facility operating under Royal Science Division oversight.

This is an unusual career trajectory. Royal Science Division promotions typically require decades of incremental advancement, political maneuvering, and careful alignment with institutional priorities. E. Gadd achieved leadership positions through what contemporary documents describe as 'exceptional practical results' — meaning he built things that worked, and the things that worked were useful to powerful people.

The Boo Insurgency of 973 BF was the inflection point. Before the insurgency, E. Gadd's research was considered academically interesting but practically limited. After the insurgency — after the Poltergust Mark I proved that ghosts could be captured, contained, and controlled — E. Gadd became essential. Funding increased. Facilities expanded. Security clearances multiplied.

By 980 BF, E. Gadd had access to resources that other researchers could not obtain: spectral specimens of unusual power, artifacts recovered from 'locations of dimensional significance,' and — according to one fragmentary budget document — 'materials requisitioned from Guild archives under Protocol 7 authority.'

Waluigi does not know what Protocol 7 is. Waluigi has found no other reference to it. But the phrase 'requisitioned from Guild archives' suggests E. Gadd had authority to demand materials from the Mages' Guild — an unusual arrangement that implies his research served interests beyond the Royal Science Division's ordinary mandate.

## The Boo Research Institute — What They Actually Did

The Boo Research Institute operated from approximately 985 BF until its decommissioning in 1028 BF. During those forty-three years, it produced:

**Classified reports:** Waluigi has found references to 247 reports produced by the Institute, of which 243 remain classified. The four unclassified reports concern 'standard spectral taxonomy,' 'recommended containment vessel specifications,' 'training protocols for Poltergust operators,' and 'dietary preferences of domesticated Boos' — the last of which Waluigi finds oddly specific and suspects was declassified as a joke.

**Contained specimens:** The Institute maintained holding facilities for captured ghosts. Capacity estimates range from 'dozens' to 'hundreds' depending on the source. One decommissioning document references 'transfer of 847 contained entities to secondary facility' — suggesting the Institute held a substantial population of ghosts and that population was moved somewhere when the Institute closed. WHERE it was moved is not specified.

**Trained personnel:** The Institute trained Poltergust operators for deployment to haunted locations. Training records indicate approximately 200 individuals completed the program over four decades. Current status of these operators is unknown — Waluigi has found no registry of certified ghost hunters, and Luigi appears to operate independently rather than as part of any organized force.

**Experimental technology:** Beyond the Poltergust series, the Institute developed devices that remain classified. One budget document references 'Project Looking Glass' — no description provided. Another references 'the Nightmare Machine' — also no description. A third references 'Boo containment matrix, Type K variant, for deployment per royal directive' — which suggests the Institute was developing specialized containment for a specific high-value target.

Waluigi suspects 'Type K' refers to King Boo, the most powerful and hostile Boo entity documented in Mushroom Kingdom records. King Boo has been captured and escaped multiple times. If E. Gadd was developing specialized containment specifically for King Boo, that research would have significant strategic value — and significant danger if it fell into wrong hands.

## Service to the Royal Family — The Hidden Timeline

Waluigi has reconstructed E. Gadd's service to the Mushroom Kingdom's royal family through fragmentary references across multiple document types. The timeline reveals a longer and more intimate relationship than public records suggest:

**955 BF — The Assassination Year:** E. Gadd was employed by the Royal Science Division and held clearances permitting access to royal facilities. His whereabouts on Highsun 1, 955 BF — the day of Princess Peach's assassination — are not documented in any record Waluigi has accessed. This could mean he was not present at the castle. This could also mean his presence was deliberately unrecorded.

**962 BF — The Star Road Collapse:** The Star Road network connecting the kingdom's major settlements was destroyed in 962 BF through means that have never been fully explained. E. Gadd's research during this period included 'dimensional stability measurements' and 'energy signature analysis of trans-planar conduits.' Waluigi cannot confirm whether E. Gadd was involved in the Star Road's destruction, its investigation, or attempts at its repair. Waluigi notes only that his expertise would have been relevant.

**978 BF — 'Technical Advisor to the Crown':** E. Gadd received this formal appointment twenty-three years AFTER Peach's assassination, during the Regency period. The appointment gave him 'direct access to royal facilities and communication channels with designated Crown representatives.' Since there WAS no Crown after Peach's death — only the Regency acting in the Crown's name — this appointment effectively made E. Gadd an advisor to the Regency itself.

**985 BF — The Emergency Session:** Waluigi has documented elsewhere that the Regency Council held a classified emergency session in 985 BF involving 'Personnel Reallocation.' E. Gadd's calendar — reconstructed from fragmentary sources — shows he was summoned to the Regency Council on the same date. What he told them, or what they told him, is unknown. Mario's public presence declined dramatically after this date. E. Gadd's security clearances INCREASED after this date.

Waluigi is not drawing conclusions. Waluigi is noting correlations.

**1001 BF — Luigi's First Mansion:** E. Gadd personally equipped and trained Luigi for the operation that became known as 'Luigi's Mansion' — the rescue of Mario from a ghost-infested building. E. Gadd provided the Poltergust 3000, the Game Boy Horror communication device, and real-time tactical support. The operation was successful. Luigi captured numerous ghosts including several 'portrait ghosts' of unusual power. E. Gadd converted the captured ghosts into portrait form using his Ghost Portrificationizer.

Waluigi notes: the ghosts captured during Luigi's Mansion were not ordinary Boos. They were the spirits of individuals who had died in the mansion — people with names, histories, and apparent personalities. E. Gadd converted these human-origin ghosts into decorative portraits. The ethical implications are uncomfortable. E. Gadd apparently did not share this discomfort, or suppressed it in favor of practical considerations.

**1025 BF — The Chaos Heart Crisis:** E. Gadd provided unspecified technical support during the events surrounding Count Bleck's attempt to destroy all dimensions using the Chaos Heart. The nature of this support is classified. What Waluigi has confirmed: E. Gadd was present at some point during the crisis. E. Gadd's equipment was used. E. Gadd's research may have been relevant to understanding dimensional collapse scenarios.

This is also when Mr. L emerged — Luigi's alternate personality, created through unknown means, serving Count Bleck's agenda. If E. Gadd was present during the crisis, he would have observed Mr. L firsthand. He would have had opportunity to study the phenomenon. He would have had motivation to develop containment or reversal protocols.

Waluigi suspects — but cannot confirm — that E. Gadd's post-crisis research focused heavily on Mr. L. The 'Protocol Green Thunder' mentioned in various documents may be a containment or emergency response procedure for Mr. L emergence. E. Gadd would have been uniquely positioned to develop such a protocol, given his expertise in spectral containment and his personal knowledge of Luigi.

**1028 BF — The Disappearance:** E. Gadd's final public appearance, the seizure of his laboratories, his removal from institutional records. Waluigi has documented this elsewhere in this entry. The timing — three years after the Chaos Heart Crisis, during a period when Mr. L was supposedly 'cured' — may be significant. E. Gadd may have discovered that the cure was incomplete. He may have discovered something about how Mr. L was created in the first place. He may have discovered something about WHO was responsible.

Or he may have simply retired. Waluigi acknowledges this possibility while finding it unsatisfying.

## The Poltergust Series — Technical Documentation

Waluigi is including comprehensive technical information about E. Gadd's most famous invention because the Poltergust remains in active use and understanding its capabilities may be relevant to ongoing investigations.

**Poltergust Mark I (973 BF):**
- Operators required: 2
- Power source: External generator (wagon-mounted)
- Effective range: 5 meters
- Containment capacity: Approximately 20 standard spectral units
- Notable features: First successful ghost-capture device; crude but functional
- Current status: Several units in museum collections; non-operational

**Poltergust Mark II (981 BF):**
- Operators required: 1
- Power source: Internal battery (backpack-mounted)
- Effective range: 10 meters
- Containment capacity: Approximately 50 standard spectral units
- Notable features: Portable design; improved suction mechanics
- Current status: Recalled in 1002 BF for 'safety retrofitting'; units never redistributed

**Poltergust 3000 (998 BF):**
- Operators required: 1
- Power source: Internal battery with elemental medallion augmentation
- Effective range: 15 meters
- Containment capacity: Approximately 100 standard spectral units
- Notable features: Elemental integration (fire, water, ice attacks); Game Boy Horror compatibility
- Current status: Limited production (fewer than 20 units); Luigi operated one during original mansion incident

**Poltergust Mark III (1015 BF):**
- Classification level: Restricted
- Operators required: Unknown
- Power source: Unknown
- Effective range: Unknown
- Containment capacity: 'Enhanced for Type K entities'
- Notable features: 'Failsafe integration per Guild request'; 'third function — L does not know'
- Current status: Unknown

Waluigi must pause on the Mark III documentation. The phrase 'third function — L does not know' appears in a fragmentary document Waluigi obtained through channels that cannot be disclosed. The phrase suggests E. Gadd built capabilities into the Mark III that were deliberately concealed from Luigi — 'L' almost certainly referring to Luigi given context.

What is the third function? Waluigi does not know. Possibilities include:

- Emergency self-destruct to prevent captured entities from being released
- Remote override allowing someone other than Luigi to control the device
- Specialized containment mode for Mr. L himself — a way to capture Luigi if his alternate personality emerges
- Something else entirely that Waluigi cannot imagine

The phrase 'failsafe integration per Guild request' suggests the Mages' Guild specifically requested this hidden capability. The Guild's involvement in E. Gadd's research has been documented elsewhere. The Guild's interest in controlling Luigi — through his Guild contract, through the warrant against him, through 'Phase One' containment protocols — has also been documented.

If the Guild requested a hidden function in Luigi's equipment, and Luigi does not know about it, then Luigi is operating with compromised tools. His Poltergust may be a containment device pointed at him as much as at the ghosts he hunts.

**Poltergust Mark IV (estimated 1022 BF):**
- Classification level: Highly Restricted
- Documentation: Single reference only
- Notable features: 'Recommended minimum for King Boo engagement'
- Current status: May not have entered production

**Poltergust G-00 (date unknown):**
- Classification level: Unknown
- Documentation: References to 'Gooigi deployment protocols'
- Notable features: Unknown
- Current status: Unknown

## Other Inventions — Comprehensive List

Waluigi has found references to the following E. Gadd inventions beyond the Poltergust series:

**Confirmed functional devices:**

- **Pixelator:** Matter-to-data conversion; development 'shelved' due to Guild concerns
- **Ghost Portrificationizer:** Converts captured ghosts to portrait form for storage
- **Dark-Light Device:** Reveals objects hidden by Spirit Ball concealment
- **Dual Scream:** Upgraded communication device replacing Game Boy Horror
- **Strobulb:** High-intensity flash attachment for stunning ghosts
- **Super Poltergust:** Variant with 'enhanced suction for emergency evacuation scenarios'
- **Virtual Boo:** Training simulation system
- **Parascope:** Deep-scan device for detecting entities through solid matter

**Devices mentioned but not described:**

- **Project Looking Glass:** Classification level exceeds Waluigi's access
- **The Nightmare Machine:** Classification level exceeds Waluigi's access
- **Temporal Displacement Compensator:** Referenced in connection with 'the 1019 incident'
- **Entity Communication Array:** 'For negotiation with non-hostile spectral entities'
- **The Portalizer:** Mentioned once; no context
- **Defensive Protocol Seven:** Not clear if this is a device or a procedure
- **Gooigi Cultivation Chamber:** Referenced in Gooigi deployment protocols

**Rumored devices — unconfirmed:**

- A device capable of 'reversing spectral transformation' — restoring ghosts to living form
- A device capable of 'personality extraction and storage' — possibly relevant to Mr. L
- A device capable of 'dimensional anchoring' — preventing planar displacement
- A 'failsafe key' that can remotely disable all Poltergust units simultaneously

Their timeline status is listed in official documents as 'indeterminate' — neither alive nor dead, neither present nor absent, neither past nor future. ## The Disappearance — Extended Analysis

Waluigi has documented the basic facts of E. Gadd's disappearance earlier in this entry. Waluigi now provides extended analysis based on additional evidence.

Gadd may have been explaining how dimensional boundaries were failing, identifying those responsible, and admitting his own complicity while proposing a solution that required unofficial action.

Three weeks later, his laboratory was seized and he vanished.

One former staff member — speaking anonymously — told Waluigi's source: 'They didn't want us to see what they were taking. They didn't want us to know what was being preserved versus destroyed. Gadd's research, the lack of insignia would be consistent with their standard practices.

The numbering suggests at least eight distinct facilities over E. Gadd's career. The gaps in documentation suggest some facilities were classified from inception. The number of decommissioned laboratories suggests E. Gadd's research repeatedly produced results that required facility abandonment.

If E. Gadd continued his work after 1028 BF — and Waluigi suspects he did — he would need a new laboratory. Lab 9, perhaps. Or multiple smaller facilities to avoid concentrating his work in one seizeable location.

Gadd fits this pattern: extract useful research, then suppress the researcher.

A disappeared researcher is an ASSET if you know where he is and others do not.

description:
Waluigi has a complicated relationship with Luigi. Waluigi does not wish to discuss this relationship in detail, but it is relevant to acknowledge that Waluigi's investigation of Mr. L is not entirely objective. Waluigi has TRIED to be objective. Waluigi has cross-referenced sources. Waluigi has questioned his own assumptions. But when investigating someone you have competed against, resented, pitied, and occasionally almost respected over decades of shared history, complete objectivity is impossible. Waluigi acknowledges this limitation and proceeds anyway.

## The Official Narrative — What Everyone Is Supposed to Believe

The Regency's official account of Mr. L is straightforward, convenient, and almost certainly incomplete. According to their records, Luigi was captured by an extradimensional entity during a period of crisis approximately fifteen years ago. This entity—variously described as 'Count Bleck's forces,' 'the Chaos Heart's influence,' or simply 'dimensional corruption'—subjected Luigi to some form of mental manipulation that created an alternate personality called Mr. L.

Mr. L was everything Luigi was not. Confident where Luigi was anxious. Aggressive where Luigi was hesitant. Cruel where Luigi was compassionate. Mr. L worked against the Mushroom Kingdom's interests, opposed Mario directly, and demonstrated combat capabilities that Luigi had never previously displayed. The official narrative emphasizes that Luigi was not responsible for Mr. L's actions—he was a victim, a puppet, a tool wielded by hostile forces beyond his control.

Eventually, according to this narrative, Mario defeated the dimensional threat, the brainwashing was broken, and Luigi returned to his normal self. Mr. L was suppressed, contained, eliminated—the terminology varies depending on which document you consult. Luigi resumed his life as the second brother, the ghost hunter, the reliable sidekick who would never again threaten the kingdom he loved.

This narrative has problems. Waluigi will enumerate them.

## Problem One — The Warrant

If Mr. L was truly eliminated fifteen years ago, why does Luigi's current arrest warrant include charges for 'residual Mr. L activities'? The warrant—issued by Magistrate Toadsworth IV in 1040 BF—specifically references 'suspected continued possession or concealment of hypnotic/brainwashing artifacts or knowledge derived from same, endangering public safety, in violation of Post-Crisis Security Order 962-D.'

This language does not describe someone who was cured and moved on. This describes someone who the Regency believes still possesses dangerous capabilities from the Mr. L period. Either the Regency is issuing warrants based on fifteen-year-old paranoia with no current evidence, or they know something about Luigi's current state that contradicts the official 'he's fine now' narrative.

Waluigi has attempted to obtain the affidavits supporting this charge. They are sealed. The sealing itself is suspicious—if the evidence is solid, why hide it? If the evidence is weak, why include the charge at all? The warrant suggests that somewhere in Regency archives, there is documentation of Mr. L-related activity occurring RECENTLY enough to justify criminal charges.

## Problem Two — Luigi's Silence

At the ruined manor convergence, Archie Miser asked Luigi directly: 'Did you do something evil?' in reference to the Mr. L period. Multiple witnesses from multiple factions confirm what happened next: Luigi went silent. He did not deny it. He did not explain it. He did not offer context or justification. He simply... stopped speaking.

This silence is devastating to the official narrative. If Luigi was truly a puppet with no agency during the Mr. L period, he would have said so. 'I wasn't in control.' 'It wasn't me.' 'I was being used.' Any of these responses would have been consistent with the brainwashing story. Instead, Luigi chose silence—the response of someone who cannot honestly deny the accusation but cannot bring himself to confirm it either.

Waluigi has considered alternative explanations for the silence. Perhaps Luigi was overwhelmed by trauma and could not respond. Perhaps Luigi was calculating his legal position and chose not to answer. Perhaps Luigi knew that anything he said would be used against him and silence was strategic.

None of these explanations are satisfying. Trauma might explain inability to discuss events, but Luigi had been discussing other charges moments before—he was capable of speech. Legal calculation might explain refusing to answer, but Luigi had already made statements that could be used against him on other charges. Strategic silence might make sense, but Luigi fled via Poltergust moments later—abandoning any strategic positioning the silence might have provided.

The simplest explanation for Luigi's silence: he did do something evil, or believes he did, and cannot bring himself to lie about it.

## Problem Three — The Capabilities Gap

Mr. L demonstrated combat capabilities that Luigi had never shown before and has rarely shown since. According to accounts from that period, Mr. L was a skilled fighter, a competent pilot of advanced machinery, a strategic thinker capable of planning and executing complex operations. He called himself 'the Green Thunder' without apparent irony and backed up the boast with performance.

The official narrative attributes these capabilities to the dimensional enhancement—whatever brainwashing Luigi underwent also unlocked latent abilities or granted new ones. When the brainwashing ended, these capabilities supposedly faded.

But Waluigi has observed Luigi in action. Waluigi has seen Luigi fight ghosts with the Poltergust, navigate dangerous situations, survive encounters that should have killed him. Luigi is more capable than his anxious demeanor suggests. The gap between 'normal Luigi' and 'Mr. L' may not be as vast as the official narrative implies.

What if the capabilities did not come from external enhancement? What if they were always present, suppressed by Luigi's anxiety and self-doubt, and the 'brainwashing' simply removed those psychological barriers? Under this interpretation, Mr. L is not a foreign personality implanted in Luigi—Mr. L is LUIGI, freed from the limitations he normally imposes on himself.

This interpretation is disturbing because it suggests the 'cure' did not eliminate Mr. L. It simply re-imposed the psychological barriers that kept Mr. L contained. Luigi walks around every day with Mr. L inside him, held back by anxiety and self-doubt that are actually PROTECTIVE rather than pathological.

If this interpretation is correct, anything that reduces Luigi's inhibitions—extreme stress, emotional crisis, magical influence—could potentially release Mr. L again. The Green Thunder is not gone. He is waiting.

## The Mario Connection — Waluigi's Most Disturbing Theory

Waluigi has been investigating Mario's disappearance extensively. The Star Fountain reunion. The Eastern Passage. The fragmentary evidence of farms and companions and peaceful deaths that may or may not have occurred. Throughout this investigation, Waluigi has treated Mario and Luigi as separate cases that occasionally intersect.

But what if they are not separate? What if Mr. L and Mario's disappearance are connected in ways that no one wants to acknowledge?

Consider the timeline. The Mr. L incident occurred approximately fifteen years ago. Mario defeated the dimensional threat and 'saved' Luigi. The brothers resumed their lives. Everything seemed normal.

Then Mario started asking about routes EAST. Then Mario disappeared. Then the Star Fountain reunion occurred—a meeting so emotional that Luigi said 'I thought I would never see you again.' Then Mario allegedly traveled further east and may have died on a farm.

Why did Mario leave? The official theories involve Guild manipulation, Regency threats, voluntary exile. But Waluigi now considers another possibility: what if Mario left because of Luigi?

Not because Luigi threatened him. Because Mario saw something in Luigi—something left over from Mr. L—that convinced him staying was impossible. Perhaps the 'cure' was not complete. Perhaps Mario witnessed Mr. L resurface in private moments. Perhaps Mario realized that his presence was the trigger—that Luigi's self-doubt was partially rooted in comparison to Mario, and removing Mario from the equation was the only way to keep Mr. L contained.

Under this theory, Mario's exile was not abandonment but PROTECTION. Mario left because staying risked awakening Mr. L permanently. The distance between the brothers—which has seemed tragic throughout Waluigi's investigation—might actually be therapeutic. Luigi is more stable when he is not constantly reminded of how much greater his brother is.

This theory is speculation. Waluigi has no direct evidence. But it would explain Mario's secrecy about his reasons for leaving. It would explain why Luigi accepts the separation instead of searching for his brother. It would explain 'he's where he needs to be'—Luigi understanding that Mario's absence is necessary for Luigi's own sanity.

## Alternative Theory — Mr. L as Independent Entity

Waluigi must also consider the possibility that Mr. L is not Luigi at all—not a suppressed personality, not an unlocked capability set, but a genuinely separate entity that inhabited Luigi's body during the dimensional crisis.

Dimensional entities have been documented throughout the Raventree crisis. The Planar Fracture demonstrated that consciousness can be displaced, merged, fragmented across dimensional boundaries. What if the 'brainwashing' narrative is not entirely wrong but is also not entirely right? What if an external entity entered Luigi during the crisis, operated his body as Mr. L, and then was supposedly expelled when Mario defeated the threat?

If this entity was not truly destroyed—if it was merely displaced or dispersed or temporarily banished—it might still exist somewhere. It might still have connection to Luigi. It might be capable of partial or complete return under the right circumstances.

The 'residual Mr. L activities' charge in Luigi's warrant could refer to this connection. Perhaps the Regency has evidence that the entity is attempting to re-establish contact. Perhaps Luigi himself has experienced moments of intrusion—hearing thoughts that are not his, feeling impulses that do not match his character, losing time he cannot account for.

If Mr. L is an independent entity rather than an aspect of Luigi, the moral calculus changes entirely. Luigi would be genuinely innocent of Mr. L's crimes—a victim rather than a perpetrator. But he would also be genuinely dangerous—a potential vessel for something hostile that could return without warning.

## The Name Question — Why 'L'?

Waluigi has always found the name 'Mr. L' significant in ways that are hard to articulate. The persona could have chosen any name. The dimensional entity—if there was one—could have called itself anything. Why 'L'?

The obvious answer: L stands for Luigi. The name references the host body, the identity being subverted, the person being controlled.

But there is another interpretation. What if L stands for something else? What if the name is not derived from Luigi but from some other source that happens to share the initial?

Waluigi does not know what this alternative source might be. Waluigi is speculating in directions that may lead nowhere. But the name 'Mr. L' has always felt deliberate—not like a random designation but like a meaningful choice. Understanding WHY that name was chosen might reveal something about the nature of the entity or personality that chose it.

## What Mr. L Actually Did — The Gaps in the Record

Waluigi has attempted to compile a complete account of Mr. L's activities during the crisis period. This has proven nearly impossible. Records from that time are fragmentary, contradictory, and in many cases deliberately obscured.

What Waluigi has been able to confirm:

Mr. L operated machinery—specifically some kind of combat robot or mechanical suit—in actions against Mushroom Kingdom forces. Casualties occurred. The exact number is classified or lost. Mr. L was not a minor threat; he was considered dangerous enough to warrant significant military response.

Mr. L worked with or for an entity associated with dimensional manipulation. The 'Chaos Heart' is mentioned in several sources. 'Count Bleck' appears in others. The exact nature of this allegiance—willing collaboration, coerced service, or complete mind control—varies depending on the source.

Mr. L confronted Mario directly at least once. The outcome of this confrontation is unclear. Some sources suggest Mario defeated Mr. L in combat. Others suggest the confrontation was more complex—negotiation, attempted rescue, or something else entirely.

Mr. L's activity period lasted weeks to months depending on which timeline you accept. This is not a brief episode. Whatever Mr. L did, he did it long enough to establish patterns, relationships, and consequences that extended well beyond a single incident.

What Waluigi cannot confirm:

How many people died as a result of Mr. L's actions? The number is either very small (Regency preferred interpretation) or very large (Loyalist accusations) depending on political motivation. The truth is probably somewhere between these extremes, but Waluigi cannot establish it.

Did Mr. L harm civilians or only military targets? Some accounts suggest deliberate cruelty toward non-combatants. Others suggest Mr. L was focused on specific objectives and avoided unnecessary casualties. The difference matters enormously for moral assessment but cannot be resolved from available evidence.

Did Mr. L have moments of apparent Luigi-consciousness during the crisis? Some witnesses claim Mr. L occasionally showed confusion, hesitation, or behaviors inconsistent with his usual persona—suggesting Luigi was still present, fighting for control. Other witnesses claim Mr. L was completely consistent throughout—suggesting total suppression of Luigi's personality. Again, Waluigi cannot determine which accounts are accurate.

Did Mr. L know about Mario's eventual intervention? Was Mr. L working toward his own liberation, or was he fully committed to the hostile agenda? The answer would reveal much about the nature of the Mr. L personality, but no available source addresses it clearly.

## The Ghost Hunting Connection

Luigi's current profession is ghost hunting. He carries the Poltergust, he pursues spectral entities, he has become expert in dealing with the dead and the dimensionally displaced. Waluigi has always assumed this was simply Luigi finding work that suited his skills while Mario was absent.

But consider an alternative interpretation: what if Luigi hunts ghosts because he understands them? What if the Poltergust is not just a weapon but a form of THERAPY—a way of confronting dimensional entities similar to whatever created Mr. L? What if Luigi's expertise in ghost capture comes from personal experience with possession or intrusion?

The Poltergust sucks up ghosts and contains them. It removes spirits from the material plane and traps them where they cannot cause harm. If Luigi fears that Mr. L might return—or that dimensional entities might attempt to influence him again—what better profession than one dedicated to capturing and containing such threats?

Under this interpretation, Luigi is not merely employed as a ghost hunter. He is PRACTICING. Every ghost he captures is a rehearsal for containing the threat within himself. Every successful Poltergust deployment reinforces his confidence that intrusive entities can be controlled.

This is speculation. But it fits the pattern of someone who has experienced dimensional violation and is determined never to experience it again.

## The Warrant's True Purpose — Waluigi's Political Theory

Waluigi has considered why the Regency would include Mr. L charges in Luigi's warrant when other charges—withholding Mario's location, Guild association, obstruction—would suffice for arrest. The Mr. L charges add complexity, invoke classified histories, and raise questions that the Regency presumably does not want publicly aired.

Unless the Mr. L charges are the actual point.

What if the Regency is not trying to arrest Luigi for obstruction or Guild association? What if they want him for Mr. L-related interrogation specifically? The other charges provide legal cover, but the real questions they want answered involve dimensional manipulation, residual connections to hostile entities, and capabilities that might be useful or dangerous in the current crisis.

The Planar Fracture has destabilized dimensional boundaries throughout the region. Entities from other planes are more active than they have been in years. If Mr. L's powers derived from dimensional connection, those powers might be more accessible now than they have been since the original crisis. Luigi—or Mr. L—might have become strategically valuable in ways that have nothing to do with Mario's location.

The Regency might want to USE Luigi. Or they might want to ensure no one else can use him. Either way, the warrant begins to look less like law enforcement and more like asset acquisition.

## What Luigi Fears — A Psychological Profile

Waluigi has observed Luigi for decades. The anxiety, the hesitation, the persistent insecurity that manifests even in situations where Luigi has demonstrated clear competence. These traits have always seemed excessive—why would someone who has survived so much, accomplished so much, still doubt himself so constantly?

Mr. L provides an answer. Luigi is afraid of HIMSELF.

Not afraid of failure, not afraid of danger, not afraid of being overshadowed by Mario. Luigi is afraid that if he lets himself feel confident, capable, powerful—if he stops doubting and starts asserting—he will become something he cannot control. The anxiety is not weakness. It is a CONTAINMENT PROTOCOL.

Luigi keeps himself small because making himself large risks becoming Mr. L.

This interpretation explains so much about Luigi's behavior. Why he deflects praise. Why he minimizes his achievements. Why he seems almost relieved when others take credit for his actions. Every acknowledgment of his power is a threat. Every moment of pride is a crack in the containment.

If Waluigi is right, Luigi is engaged in constant psychological warfare against a part of himself that wants OUT. And he has been fighting this war for fifteen years, alone, without acknowledgment or support, because admitting the war exists would mean admitting that Mr. L is not gone.

## The Silence Revisited

Waluigi returns to the moment at the ruined manor. Archie asks if Luigi did something evil as Mr. L. Luigi goes silent.

Waluigi now believes the silence was not evasion or trauma or legal calculation. The silence was HONESTY.

Luigi could not say 'yes, I did evil' because acknowledging Mr. L's actions as his own would validate the interpretation that Mr. L is part of Luigi rather than an external intrusion. It would make Luigi responsible for things he experienced as violation.

Luigi could not say 'no, I did not do evil' because he REMEMBERS. Whatever dissociation the brainwashing provided, Luigi apparently retains some awareness of what Mr. L did. He cannot honestly deny it because he was there—trapped inside, screaming in the back seat, but THERE.

Luigi could not explain the complexity because explanation would take hours, would reveal classified information, would expose vulnerabilities that dangerous parties could exploit. In the middle of a battlefield with multiple factions listening, detailed psychological excavation was impossible.

So Luigi said nothing. And then he fled. And now he is somewhere unknown, carrying guilt he cannot express for actions he may or may not have been responsible for, with a warrant charging him with activities related to the darkest period of his life.

Waluigi does not know whether to pity Luigi or fear him. Waluigi suspects the appropriate response is both.

## Final Assessment

Mr. L remains one of the most troubling mysteries in Waluigi's investigation. The official narrative is clearly incomplete. The alternative interpretations are disturbing in different ways. The truth probably combines elements from multiple theories—partial brainwashing, partial suppressed personality, partial independent entity, partial capability unlocking. Dimensional phenomena rarely fit neat categories.

What Waluigi believes with reasonable confidence:

Mr. L was not entirely external to Luigi. Something about Luigi's own psychology, capabilities, or identity was involved in the Mr. L persona. The 'pure brainwashing' narrative is too simple.

Mr. L did things that Luigi cannot comfortably acknowledge. The silence at the manor confirms this. Whether Luigi was morally responsible for these actions is a separate question from whether they occurred.

Mr. L is not completely gone. The warrant's charges, Luigi's ongoing anxiety, the strategic interest various factions show in Luigi—all suggest that Mr. L or his capabilities remain relevant to current events.

The connection to Mario's disappearance is possible but unproven. Waluigi's theory about Mario leaving to protect Luigi from himself is speculation based on circumstantial evidence. It could be completely wrong. But it fits the available data better than competing explanations.

Luigi is dangerous in ways that his demeanor obscures. The anxious ghost hunter is also the Green Thunder—not was, IS. Whatever containment Luigi has built for himself is psychological rather than magical, and psychological containment can fail.

Waluigi will continue investigating Mr. L as part of the broader investigation into Luigi, Mario, and the assassination conspiracy. The connections between these mysteries grow more apparent with each new piece of evidence. Mr. L may be the key to understanding what really happened to the Mario Brothers and why one disappeared while the other cannot stop running.

Or Mr. L may be exactly what the official narrative claims—a closed chapter, a resolved crisis, a cured condition that poses no ongoing threat. The Regency would prefer everyone believe this interpretation. The warrant they issued suggests they do not believe it themselves.

Waluigi does not know what to believe. Waluigi knows only that Luigi's silence speaks louder than any testimony, and that somewhere behind those anxious eyes, the Green Thunder might still be watching.

WAH.

**Backfilled from 2 Aethel, 1035 BF — the first witness record.** Years after the Regency closed his file, two witnesses in a helicopter watched a man in black and lime green — Luigi's overalls, Luigi's cap, a black mask — standing in the main street outside Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic reciting verse at a courier. The courier shot him. He did not fall. He lengthened: arms past the shape of arms, hands with too many knuckles, eyes lit red, a mouth wider than a face allows. A mouth opened in the road beside him — out of the ground, not out of him — and he stood beside it like a man beside his own car. One hand threw the courier through the clinic's front window. Twenty minutes later, on the storehouse stairs next door, there were three of him, laughing without sound, watching two men fight over a notebook. He followed nobody. He harmed only the man who shot him first. He let the two signatories of a sixty-thirty contract leave, and a single copy of him faded through the lamplight by the stairwell door, checking his own fingers as it went. The verse carried the words bridge, brother, and debt. The archive files what was heard, not what it means — and it notes that the informant's report that night put Luigi unconscious in the clinic's private wing, behind the window the thing in his clothes was standing outside.
