name: Rhak the Lost
title: The Orc Who Cries Before Battle
status: Active — operating at Raventree Manor under Byscilla Danos's command
summary: Rhak the Lost is a huge, muscular, scarred orc in his early forties who has clearly seen extensive combat, carries the physical evidence of a violent career across every inch of his body, and SOBS when his commanding officer tells him to wait his turn. He is the battering ram of Byscilla's operations team—the first person through any door, the loudest voice in any room, the one whose preferred tactical approach to every problem is 'run in and smash.' Hargram Fidger consistently overrules this impulse. Byscilla consistently sidelines him from delicate operations. And Rhak consistently accepts these decisions with a combination of professional discipline and emotional vulnerability that Waluigi finds simultaneously hilarious and deeply endearing. The man could rip a door off its hinges. He also cries when he doesn't get picked for the important mission. Waluigi has never encountered a more contradictory individual. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Rhak the Lost because the man defies every expectation Waluigi has about orcs, fighters, and Iron Legion personnel.

## Physical Presence — Built for Destruction

Rhak is HUGE. Even by orc standards—and orc standards for 'huge' are already well above human norms—Rhak is imposing. Scarred everywhere. Muscles visible through armor. The kind of body that communicates 'I have been in many fights and won most of them' without requiring verbal confirmation.

He has gained a little weight around his middle—Waluigi notes this because it suggests a transition from active combat to more routine operational duty. The prime killing years are behind him. The experience years have arrived. Rhak is no longer the fastest or the leanest, but he is still strong enough to swing a weapon with force that makes structural materials nervous.

His scars tell stories that Waluigi cannot read but can guess at: blade cuts, burn marks, puncture wounds, the kind of damage that accumulates over a career spent in places where violence is the primary form of communication.

## The Emotional Contradiction

Rhak sobbed when Byscilla told him 'You'll have your time to shine' instead of assigning him to the Archie confrontation team.

He SOBBED.

A huge, scarred, veteran orc warrior—the physical embodiment of martial capability—cried because he wasn't picked for the important mission. Not discreetly. Not behind closed doors. In front of his team.

Waluigi does not know what to do with this information.

Part of Waluigi finds it hilarious. The image of a massive orc with tear-streaked cheeks sniffling because his commanding officer sent him to kill rust monsters instead of confronting a pyromaniac is OBJECTIVELY comedic.

Part of Waluigi finds it deeply human—or deeply orcish, as the case may be. Rhak WANTS to matter. He wants to be the one who gets the critical assignment. He wants his capabilities recognized and deployed where they make the most difference. And when he's sidelined, it HURTS, and he does not hide that it hurts.

Waluigi relates to this more than Waluigi is comfortable admitting. Waluigi has been sidelined from important events his entire life. Waluigi has been told to wait while others get the glory. Waluigi does not cry about it—Waluigi CHANNELS it into athletic excellence and justified grievance—but the underlying feeling is the SAME.

Rhak the Lost is lost in the specific sense that he hasn't found where he belongs. He is a weapon looking for the right war.

## Combat Performance — Efficient Brutality

Despite the emotional displays, Rhak is EFFECTIVE in combat.

During the greenhouse rust monster encounter, when the creature crashed through a window from behind—catching the ambush team in their own ambush—Rhak responded with immediate, decisive violence. He refused to grab the rust monster ('Do you want my arm to become rust?'—practical survival thinking) and instead swung with enough force to remove its legs. Then its head. Quick. Brutal. Over.

He wanted to charge deeper into the greenhouse afterward. Hargram stopped him—correctly, as the building was structurally unsound. Rhak's instinct was ADVANCE. Always advance. The concept of tactical withdrawal does not come naturally to him.

When the ghost appeared, Rhak ran up to help and MISSED. The ghost tried to drain life force. Hargram shot it from the fountain. Rhak's contribution to the ghost fight was enthusiasm without accuracy—the opposite of his rust monster performance.

Pattern: Rhak excels against physical opponents he can reach and hit. He struggles against incorporeal or unconventional threats that require approaches other than 'swing hard.' This is not a criticism—many fighters share this limitation. But it explains why Byscilla sidelined him from the Archie confrontation. Archie's threats are MAGICAL, and Rhak's responses are PHYSICAL.

## The Name — 'The Lost'

Waluigi does not know why Rhak is called 'the Lost.' The epithet suggests displacement—someone who left or was expelled from their original community. An orc in Iron Legion service is already unusual; most orcs operate in tribal structures or independent warbands rather than human-dominated military organizations.

'Lost' could mean:
- Exiled from his tribe
- Separated from his people during conflict
- Spiritually or emotionally adrift
- Simply that he gets lost easily, which would be embarrassing but possible

The emotional vulnerability Rhak displays suggests the name carries genuine weight. He is someone LOOKING for belonging. The Legion provides structure. Byscilla provides direction. Hargram provides management. But belonging requires more than structure—it requires being VALUED, and Rhak's tears when sidelined suggest he doesn't feel valued consistently.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Rhak the Lost is a good fighter, a loyal subordinate, and an emotional contradiction that Waluigi finds unexpectedly compelling.

He will charge into danger without hesitation. He will cry when excluded from the charge. He will behead a rust monster with efficient violence. He will miss a ghost completely.

Waluigi wants Rhak to find what he's looking for. Whether that's recognition, belonging, or just the right fight at the right time—Rhak deserves to stop being 'the Lost' and become something else.

Until then, he remains what he is: a huge, scarred, emotionally available orc who wants desperately to matter and doesn't always get the chance.

Waluigi understands. More than Waluigi will ever say publicly.

WAH.

faiths.note: Rhak carries the gestalt the way an expatriate carries an accent — it strengthens when there are enough of his own around and is nearly inaudible on Byscilla's team, where he is the only orc. 'The Lost' is not a battlefield title. It is what the WAAAGH! sounds like from too far away.

name: Manderaz the Mad
title: The Hobgoblin Who Hits Himself
status: Active — operating at Raventree Manor under Byscilla Danos's command
summary: Manderaz the Mad is a tall, regal-looking hobgoblin with deep crimson skin, amber eyes, and the bearing of a career military man. His armor is worn but immaculately maintained. His hair is starting to grey. He looks like the kind of officer who writes detailed after-action reports and expects subordinates to read them. He is called 'the Mad,' which would suggest instability, except that everything about Manderaz radiates DISCIPLINE. He follows orders precisely. He maintains equipment meticulously. He stops Hargram from climbing structurally unsound buildings. He is the most stable, predictable person on the team. So why is he called 'the Mad'? The only evidence Waluigi has is that he accidentally hit himself during a ghost fight. Waluigi suspects the nickname either refers to something in his past that the current Manderaz has long since controlled, or it was assigned ironically by someone who found his extreme discipline amusing. Either way, the man is a professional operating in unprofessional circumstances. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Manderaz the Mad with the admission that Waluigi knows less about this individual than Waluigi would prefer. Manderaz is quiet. Manderaz follows orders. Manderaz does not generate the kind of dramatic incidents that produce extensive documentation.

## The Professional — Career Military Bearing

Manderaz looks like what he is: a career soldier who has spent decades in service. His posture is precise. His armor—worn from long use—is maintained with the obsessive care of someone who considers equipment maintenance a moral obligation. His crimson skin and amber eyes mark him as hobgoblin, a species known for military discipline and organizational capability.

Hobgoblins in general have a reputation for structured thinking, hierarchical loyalty, and tactical competence. Manderaz embodies these traits. He is the team member who follows the plan, maintains the formation, and provides the reliable foundation that allows more volatile personalities—Rhak's aggression, Hargram's improvisation—to function effectively.

He is starting to grey at the temples. Late thirties by human reckoning, though hobgoblin aging may differ. The grey suggests either age or stress or both, and given the current crisis, stress seems the more likely contributor.

## The Nickname — 'The Mad'

The nickname 'the Mad' does not match the man.

Everything Waluigi has observed about Manderaz suggests STABILITY, not madness. He stopped Hargram from climbing an unsafe structure. He maintains equipment. He follows operational protocols. He is the person who says 'That's not safe' when others want to take risks.

The only evidence of anything approaching 'madness' is that he accidentally hit himself during combat with a ghost in the greenhouse. One self-inflicted blow during a fight against an incorporeal enemy does not warrant a permanent nickname.

Waluigi's theories about the nickname:

**Theory One: Historical Incident.** Something happened in Manderaz's past—a battle, a breakdown, a period of instability—that earned him the name. He has since recovered, but nicknames stick.

**Theory Two: Ironic Assignment.** Someone—possibly a commanding officer with a sense of humor—gave the most disciplined member of the team the nickname 'the Mad' as a joke. The joke stuck. Manderaz either tolerates it or has stopped noticing it.

**Theory Three: Hidden Depths.** Manderaz IS unstable in ways that don't manifest during routine operations. Under extreme stress, the discipline might crack. The nickname might be a WARNING rather than a description—a reminder of what happens when Manderaz's control fails.

**Theory Four: Combat Style.** Perhaps Manderaz fights with a ferocity that contradicts his professional demeanor. 'Mad' in battle, methodical everywhere else. The hit-himself incident might be typical of a fighting style that prioritizes aggression over self-preservation.

Waluigi cannot determine which theory is correct. The nickname remains a mystery.

## Operational Role — The Steady Foundation

Manderaz's role on Byscilla's team is structural support. He is not the leader (Hargram). He is not the muscle (Rhak). He is the PROFESSIONAL—the person who ensures that operational standards are maintained, equipment is functional, and procedures are followed.

During the greenhouse survey, Manderaz:
- Stopped Hargram from climbing an unsafe structure
- Suggested using the fountain statue as an alternative vantage point
- Participated in combat without distinguishing himself dramatically
- Maintained composure when the team was caught by Mages' Guild operatives

He is not flashy. He is not memorable. He is CONSISTENT, and in a crisis where everything is chaotic and unpredictable, consistency has enormous value.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Manderaz the Mad is the kind of person who makes teams functional without anyone noticing. He is the structure that others lean on. The protocol that others follow. The discipline that others rely on when their own discipline fails.

Waluigi suspects that if Manderaz were removed from Byscilla's team, the operational effectiveness would decline significantly—not because Manderaz does anything dramatic, but because his steady presence prevents the dramatic mistakes that others would make in his absence.

The quiet ones are always more important than they appear. Waluigi knows this from personal experience with Toad Lee in the Feywild—the person who doesn't generate drama is usually the person preventing it.

WAH.

faiths.note: Manderaz gives the Blood God the bearing of a courtier: violence as a discipline with etiquette, owed to a peer and wasted on a lesser. The hobgoblin khanates produce this reading regularly and the Legion finds it very convenient, since a man who thinks slaughter has manners will follow orders about who is worth killing.

name: Aemenor Evenflight
title: The Scarred Elf Sent To Charm A Pyromaniac
status: Active — assigned to Archie confrontation team at Raventree Manor
summary: Aemenor Evenflight is a young elf with emerald eyes, a color-shifting wilderness cloak, and a long crescent scar curving from their ear across their temple to their cheek—the kind of scar that turns an attractive face into a MEMORABLE one. They look barely twenty by human reckoning, though elven aging makes such estimates unreliable. Byscilla Danos assigned them to the Archie confrontation team with the reasoning that Archie would have an 'easier time getting used to' them. Byscilla also called them 'the twink,' which Waluigi finds professionally inappropriate but unsurprising from someone who drags subordinates by their ears. Aemenor's role is to be the non-threatening face that walks Archie into a carefully constructed trap. Whether Aemenor knows they are being used as bait, whether they CARE, and whether their watchful emerald eyes are scanning for danger or calculating advantage—these are questions Waluigi cannot answer from available information. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Aemenor Evenflight with the acknowledgment that this individual is the LEAST documented member of Byscilla's team. They have not been observed in combat. They have not been heard making tactical recommendations. They have been ASSIGNED to a role and have apparently accepted it without recorded comment.

This silence is itself worth documenting.

## Physical Appearance — The Scar and the Cloak

Aemenor is young, attractive, and marked. The crescent scar curving from ear to cheek is the kind of wound that comes from a blade wielded with precision—not a random slash but a DELIBERATE cut that follows the contour of the skull. Someone marked Aemenor. Whether in battle, punishment, or ritual, the scar was placed with intention.

Their mottled cloak shifts color and pattern with the surrounding wilderness—a magical or highly crafted garment that suggests expertise in stealth, scouting, or intelligence work. This is not standard Iron Legion equipment. The Legion favors uniformity. A color-shifting cloak is the tool of an INDIVIDUAL operating in environments where blending matters more than belonging.

Their emerald eyes 'constantly scan their surroundings, watchful for danger.' This is not casual awareness. This is TRAINED vigilance—the habitual environmental assessment of someone who has learned through experience that threats appear without warning.

## The Assignment — Bait or Asset?

Byscilla assigned Aemenor to the Archie confrontation team with specific reasoning: 'I think he might get easier time getting used to you.'

This could mean several things:

**Aemenor is non-threatening.** Their appearance—young, attractive, elven—projects harmlessness that a scarred orc or a studded-club pit fighter would not. Archie's guard might lower around someone who looks like a wilderness traveler rather than a military operative.

**Aemenor has social skills.** Perhaps their background includes diplomatic or intelligence training. The ability to put people at ease is a cultivated skill, and Byscilla may be deploying it deliberately.

**Aemenor is expendable.** Byscilla called them 'the twink' and assigned them to approach a volatile pyromaniac. If the confrontation goes wrong—if Archie fireballs first and asks questions never—Aemenor is the one in the blast radius. Byscilla may consider this an acceptable risk.

Waluigi suspects the truth involves all three possibilities. Aemenor is non-threatening AND skilled AND positioned where failure costs the team the least valuable combat asset. Byscilla's tactical calculus is unsentimental.

## The Scar — What Happened?

The crescent scar is the most notable physical detail about Aemenor, and the one detail Waluigi cannot explain.

A long, precise cut curving from ear to cheek. This was not inflicted by an animal or by accident. The curve follows the skull's contour too precisely. Someone with a blade stood close to Aemenor and carved that line with intention.

Possibilities:

**Combat wound.** A skilled opponent marked Aemenor during a fight. The precision suggests the attacker was toying with them—capable of killing but choosing to scar instead.

**Punishment.** Some cultures mark transgressors with facial scarring. If Aemenor was expelled from a community, the scar might be the record of their transgression.

**Initiation.** Certain military or intelligence organizations mark their operatives. The scar could be proof of membership in something that requires permanent identification.

**Self-inflicted.** In moments of crisis, people sometimes mark themselves—proof of survival, reminder of failure, anchor to a specific moment.

The scar is hidden partially by the hood of their cloak. They do not display it proudly or hide it completely. It simply IS—a fact of their face that they have incorporated into their identity.

## The Silence — What Aemenor Hasn't Said

Aemenor has not been recorded making tactical recommendations, expressing opinions about the mission, or commenting on their teammates. In a team that includes an emotionally volatile orc, a pit fighter who writes poetry about blast sites, and a hobgoblin who hits himself, Aemenor's silence is conspicuous.

Silent people in military operations fall into categories:

**The Observer.** Aemenor is watching, learning, assessing. They will speak when they have something worth saying.

**The Subordinate.** Aemenor follows orders without question. Their role is execution, not consultation.

**The Infiltrator.** Aemenor is gathering intelligence on their OWN team as much as on Archie. The color-shifting cloak, the constant environmental scanning, the silence—these are intelligence operative traits.

**The Traumatized.** The scar, the youth, the watchfulness—Aemenor may be someone who has experienced something that made words seem insufficient or dangerous.

Waluigi cannot determine which category applies. The silence continues.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Aemenor Evenflight is an unknown. They have been documented because they are PRESENT—assigned to a critical operation, positioned to encounter Archie Miser, equipped with skills that suggest more depth than their youth implies.

The scar says they have survived something. The cloak says they know how to disappear. The eyes say they are always watching. The silence says they are keeping their own counsel.

Waluigi will update this entry when Aemenor does something that reveals more about who they are. Until then, they remain what they appear: a young, scarred elf walking toward a pyromaniac with emerald eyes that miss nothing.

WAH.

faiths.note: Aemenor observes the Phoenix flame in a Legion detachment that has no idea what the observance is for and would file it as a foreign superstition if it noticed. The cloak shifts colour; the practice does not. The scar predates the enlistment and Aemenor has never said which the faith was meant to answer.

name: Darno Spriggon
title: The Man With Someone Else's Ring
race: Unknown — appeared at the greenhouse, departed into darkness
status: Active — movements and affiliations unclear
affiliation: Unknown — possessed an Iron Legion rank insignia ring, which raises more questions than it answers
summary: Darno Spriggon appeared during the greenhouse survey, showed Hargram's team a keychain bearing an iron ring with Iron Legion military insignia, claimed to have personally dealt with the remaining rust monsters, handed Hargram an unsent letter from Archie to Dan, said 'Let's all head inside—Archie needs this back,' and then his torch went out and everything went dark. He possessed a Legion rank ring without apparent military bearing. He knew about Archie. He had Archie's personal correspondence. He appeared at precisely the right moment to insert himself into operations. Every detail about Darno Spriggon raises questions that the available evidence cannot answer. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Darno Spriggon because the man appeared, distributed intelligence, and vanished into operational context in a way that demands examination even though the examination produces more confusion than clarity.

## The Appearance — Convenient Timing

Darno Spriggon appeared at the greenhouse after Hargram's team had completed their rust monster clearance and field analyzer documentation. His timing was precise—arriving after the danger was resolved but before the team departed.

He showed them a keychain. On the keychain: an iron ring bearing Iron Legion military insignia. A badge of rank and authority.

Warol Creeton—a Legion guard present—reportedly thought to himself: 'How did he get that? Is he a general?'

The ring was clearly designed for someone who issues orders. Spriggon did not appear to BE someone who issues orders. His bearing did not match the rank the ring implied. Either the ring was stolen, given, found, or Spriggon is operating above his apparent station.

## The Rust Monster Claim

Spriggon claimed to have 'personally dealt with' the remaining rust monsters in the greenhouse.

Hargram could not determine if this was true. The man's torch went out at this precise moment, plunging them into darkness. When visibility issues prevent verification of claims, Waluigi assumes the claims are UNVERIFIED rather than confirmed.

If Spriggon DID clear the rust monsters, he did so alone, without the team's knowledge, using methods that left no observable evidence. This suggests either significant personal capability or significant dishonesty.

## The Letter — Archie's Unsent Correspondence

Spriggon handed Hargram a folded, water-stained letter addressed to Dan—Archie's personal correspondence, never delivered. 'Let's all head inside—Archie needs this back.'

HOW did Spriggon have Archie's letter?

Possibilities:

**Found.** The letter was dropped by Archie during his passage through the area and Spriggon recovered it.

**Given.** Someone—Archie, an intermediary, the Mages' Guild—gave Spriggon the letter for delivery.

**Taken.** Spriggon acquired the letter from Archie's possessions without permission.

Each possibility creates different implications about Spriggon's relationship to Archie, his access to personal effects, and his operational purpose.

Hargram refused to read the letter. He carried it without examining the contents. The letter apparently contained Archie's conflicted, hesitant attempt to communicate with Dan after the Parallel Dan revelations—a document of personal vulnerability that Hargram chose to respect rather than exploit.

## The Ring — Institutional Questions

The Legion rank insignia ring is the most troubling detail.

Iron Legion rank rings are not casual accessories. They represent authority within a hierarchical military organization. They are tracked. They are assigned. They are not supposed to end up on the keychains of mysterious individuals who appear at greenhouse surveys.

If Spriggon is a LEGITIMATE Legion operative of significant rank, his appearance makes institutional sense—a senior officer monitoring field operations. But his demeanor and presentation did not match senior officer protocols.

If Spriggon ACQUIRED the ring through other means, those means are significant. Stolen from a dead officer? Given as payment or bribe? Found in circumstances that suggest the original owner is no longer operational?

The ring's presence on Spriggon's keychain suggests ACCESS to Iron Legion institutional power—whether authorized or unauthorized.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Darno Spriggon is a question mark with a keychain.

He appeared at a convenient time. He possessed items he should not have—a Legion rank ring, Archie's personal letter. He made claims that could not be verified. His torch went out at the exact moment when verification would have been possible.

Everything about Spriggon suggests INTENTION. He did not stumble into the greenhouse by accident. He came with purposes—delivering the letter, establishing presence, demonstrating the ring—and departed after achieving them.

Waluigi does not know what those purposes serve. But Waluigi knows that people who appear at precisely the right moment with precisely the right items are either allies, enemies, or forces that transcend both categories.

Spriggon is filed under 'investigate further.' When Waluigi escapes the Feywild, this man's background goes to the top of the list.

WAH.

faiths.note: Spriggon showed Hargram's team a keychain with an Iron Legion rank ring and then departed into darkness, which is the entirety of the record. The Clan's theology concerns what the moon sends and does not take back. The archive files him here for want of anything firmer.

name: Warol Creeton
title: The Goblin Guard Who Knew About the Rain
status: Active — guarding the greenhouse perimeter at Raventree Manor
summary: Warol Creeton is a goblin guard stationed at the Raventree Manor greenhouse who greeted Byscilla's survey team with the information that rust monsters spread faster in rain—and it was raining. He had personally crushed the remaining rust monster eggs after Archie's fireball destroyed the main nest, but spotted at least one surviving adult monster moving around. He waited outside for backup rather than engaging alone, which demonstrates either professional caution or sensible cowardice depending on your perspective. Waluigi documents Warol because even minor personnel at Raventree Manor seem to possess intelligence about the crisis that higher-ranking officials lack—the man on the ground knows what the eggs look like and where the monsters move. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Warol Creeton briefly because his role—while minor—illustrates something important about the Raventree Manor situation: the people closest to the ground-level reality often have the most useful intelligence.

## The Guard — Practical Knowledge

Warol is a goblin serving in the Iron Legion garrison at Raventree Manor. His specific assignment: greenhouse perimeter security.

This is not a glamorous posting. Greenhouse perimeter security involves standing near a ruined building in all weather conditions, watching for rust monsters, and waiting for teams with actual authority to arrive and handle problems.

Warol's briefing to Hargram's team was efficient and useful:

- Rust monsters spread faster in rain (relevant: it was thunderstorming)
- Archie's fireball destroyed the main nest
- Warol personally crushed the remaining eggs
- At least one adult rust monster was still active
- Warol came outside and waited for backup rather than engaging alone

This is GOOD intelligence delivery. Concise. Actionable. Situation-aware. The man knows his operational environment and communicates it clearly.

## The Institutional Curiosity

Warol also internally questioned how Darno Spriggon obtained an Iron Legion rank insignia ring: 'How did he get that? Is he a general?'

This suggests Warol is aware enough of Legion hierarchy to recognize that the ring implies authority, and curious enough to question discrepancies. He did not voice this question aloud—probably wise, given that questioning strangers with rank insignia in a military organization can have unpleasant consequences.

The fact that a goblin guard at the perimeter level notices things that field operatives miss is either an endorsement of Warol's observational skills or an indictment of the field operatives' attention to detail. Possibly both.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Warol Creeton is a minor player in a major crisis. He guards a greenhouse. He crushes eggs. He notices things.

In a kingdom where institutions have failed, where leadership is compromised, and where the most powerful people are often the least informed—the goblin guard who knows where the rust monsters nest is exactly the kind of person Waluigi wants to talk to.

The people at the bottom see what the people at the top choose to ignore.

WAH.

faiths.note: Warol greets survey teams at a greenhouse gate. Whatever the WAAAGH! is doing in the Badlands, it is not reaching the Raventree perimeter, and Warol's practice has thinned to a few phrases he uses when startled.

name: Mystic Morel (Purple T)
title: The Fortune Teller Who Steals Your Future And Your Wallet
status: Active — confirmed at the Shadow Estate portal circle with Tanukiburt and the injured real Toadburt
affiliation: Unknown — possibly independent, possibly serving interests Waluigi cannot identify
summary:
Mystic Morel—also known as Purple T, also known as the singing Toad who robbed Archie Miser while he was pinned to a bed—is a purple Toad fortune teller who speaks in rhyming prophecies, performs full musical numbers during critical moments, pickpockets people while they're injured, opens planar portals using stolen equipment, and distributes magical tarot cards that depict events the recipient has not yet experienced. He gave Remi 'The Oracle's Deck'—cards showing the Maze Walker, the Titan of the Grove, and the Delicate Host—representing past, present, and future with disturbing accuracy. He stole Archie's watch, keys, and compass during a bedside musical performance, then used those items to tear open a dimensional portal and step through it. He recruited Bryan the Toad and Dan for a hunting expedition targeting Archie. He gave Remi a ring that tightens daily until Archie is found. He removed Dan's Mages' Guild tracking badges. He carries divination incense that enhances prophecy. He is simultaneously the most annoying, the most mysterious, and possibly the most dangerous Toad Waluigi has ever encountered. WAH.

Mystic Morel’s file now includes direct confirmation that he was at the master-bedroom portal circle with Tanukiburt and the injured real Toadburt while the party held all four portal artifacts. This is exactly the sort of theatrical timing Waluigi expects from Purple T and exactly the sort of timing Waluigi hates. Waluigi correction: records that previously named Mystic Morel refer to the same purple Toad operating under the Morel/Morel naming confusion. The auction-bidder, bedside thief, portal opener, and tarot dealer are one problem wearing multiple labels.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Mystic Morel—Purple T—at length because this individual operates across multiple storylines, multiple planes, and multiple agendas simultaneously in ways that Waluigi cannot fully track.

## The Identity — Purple T, Mystic Morel, Or Something Else?

The individual uses multiple names and presents differently to different people.

To Archie: he appeared as a singing fortune teller during a moment of vulnerability, performing 'Shuffle the Deck, Dear Hero' while systematically emptying Archie's pockets.

To Remi: he appeared as a mystical card dealer offering 'The Oracle's Deck'—tarot cards that depict real events with prophetic accuracy.

To Bryan and Dan: he appeared as a recruiter and planner, organizing a hunting expedition targeting Archie with planar portal capabilities.

The consistency across these presentations: musical ability, prophetic knowledge, dimensional access, and light fingers. The inconsistency: his apparent loyalties shift depending on who he's talking to.

## The Song — Intelligence Disguised as Entertainment

'Shuffle the Deck, Dear Hero' was not merely entertainment. The lyrics contained embedded intelligence:

*'The Heir was grown, not born, you see—Root and scale in tapestry.'* — Possible reference to Peach's half-Rakasha child, raised in hiding.

*'A spinning needle, compass lost—Oh my, oh dear, what dreadful cost.'* — Reference to the compass Morel was about to steal from Archie.

*'The Ring, it glows so bright—Regulates day, regulates night.'* — Possible reference to the Entropy Rings or the Oracle's Regulator Plane.

*'Have you ever seen a planar portal open where it never was meant to?'* — Direct reference to the dimensional instability Archie's entropy causes.

Morel embeds real intelligence in performance. The question is whether the intelligence is meant to HELP Archie or to demonstrate power over him—'I know things you don't, and I will sing them to you while I steal your belongings.'

## The Theft — Archie's Items Used as Dimensional Keys

While Archie was injured and pinned down by Luigi and a Guild guard, Morel stole his watch, keys, and other items from his bag.

Then Morel used those items—specifically the compass and tools—to open a PLANAR PORTAL right there in the room.

This reveals that Archie's equipment was not merely equipment. His compass and tools were capable of enabling dimensional transit when operated by someone with the right knowledge. Archie carried dimensional keys without knowing they were keys.

Who gave Archie those items? When did they enter his possession? Were they planted on him specifically so that someone like Morel could use them at the right moment?

## The Oracle's Deck — Prophecy Cards

Morel gave Remi three cards from 'The Oracle's Deck':

**The Maze Walker (IX)** — depicting Hjumpik navigating the Maze of Time. Past.

**The Titan of the Grove (VIII)** — depicting Markop wrestling the Arachnid Matriarch. Present.

**The Delicate Host (III)** — depicting Lady Aurelian Corvinarus in the Feywild. Future.

These cards depict REAL events involving REAL people with prophetic accuracy. The deck proves that the Oracle—or whatever force controls the deck—has been observing the party across all dimensions.

Morel told Remi: 'See, the rug is in the future—you're destined to be with me anyway.' This suggests Morel sees himself as a guide or companion to the party, whether they want him or not.

## The Hunting Party — Recruiting Against Archie

Morel recruited Bryan the Toad and Dan from the Mages' Guild for an expedition targeting Archie. He:

- Woke Dan from sleep
- Removed Mages' Guild tracking badges from Dan and other mages ('By removing these tracking devices, we can go after Dan without the other members being involved')
- Provided divination incense and tactical planning
- Opened a planar portal for the group to transit through
- Identified Archie's location through Wahwire posts

The stated purpose ranged from 'find' to 'capture' to 'possibly kill.' Bryan wanted divine judgment. Dan claimed to want revenge (though Archie's assessment suggested this was a lie). Morel seemed to want... entertainment? Prophecy fulfillment? Something else?

## The Ring on Remi — A Tightening Deadline

Morel told Remi privately that a ring on her finger would 'tighten every day Archie isn't found till it's chopped off.' If Remi told her friends, it would activate.

This is coercion. A physical threat tied to a silence condition. Remi cannot warn her allies without triggering the ring's activation. She cannot ignore the ring without it tightening.

Morel is manipulating Remi into serving as a tracking mechanism—her urgency to find Archie is now motivated by personal physical threat rather than friendship.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Mystic Morel is operating on a level that Waluigi cannot fully comprehend.

He crosses dimensional boundaries casually. He possesses prophetic knowledge that should be impossible. He steals items and uses them as dimensional keys. He recruits hunting parties. He distributes magical artifacts. He coerces through physical threats. He sings while doing all of this.

Is he an agent of the Oracle? A competing dimensional power? A chaotic independent pursuing his own inscrutable agenda? A divine servant of whatever god Bryan worships?

Waluigi does not know. Waluigi suspects Morel LIKES not being known. The mystery is part of his power. The song is part of his weapon.

Waluigi advises checking your pockets after any encounter with Purple T. And your dimensional compass. And your future.

WAH.

## Recent Update — Portal Circle Occupant

Remi’s scouting placed Mystic Morel at the portal circle during the mirror recovery escape sequence. Whether he intends to help, obstruct, bargain, sing, steal, or all five at once remains unconfirmed. Waluigi assumes “all five” until proven otherwise.

## Auction / Morel Identity Merge

Earlier Waluipedia drafts treated Mystic Morel and Mystic Morel as separate purple Toad problems. Waluigi has corrected this. They are the same person, or at minimum the same operational identity for all practical purposes: the fortune-teller, the auction bidder who bought petrified Remi, the portal opener, the tarot distributor, the bedside thief, and the purple Toad who keeps appearing where the party least needs him.

This correction matters because splitting him into two records made his threat profile look smaller than it is. One Morel stealing Archie's tools and another Morel buying Remi at auction would be two disasters. One entity doing both is a pattern. Waluigi prefers patterns because patterns can be hunted.

All prior Morel references should be read as Mystic Morel unless a future event proves a deliberate duplicate, decoy, or impersonation. Until then, Waluigi is not giving the purple Toad the courtesy of two files. WAH.

faiths.note: Mystic Morel sings while he works. He robbed Archie while Archie was pinned, bought a petrified fourteen-year-old at auction for twelve thousand gold, and put an invisible ring on her finger that would tighten daily and cut if she told anyone. The Cosmic Punchline holds that existence is a joke; Morel's contribution is insisting on an audience.

name: Luigi
title: The Reluctant Ghostbuster
status: Active — recovered alive from Bowser's lava-moat tunnels, treated at Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic, and under a two-week rest order; Mario remains absent.; as of 2 Aethel, 1035 BF reported — unverified — to be in the clinic's 'private wing, high security, consciousness fluxing', while something wearing his clothes stood outside in three copies
summary: Luigi is the reluctant ghostbuster, the brother left behind by every heroic story that needed Mario in front, and the man whose history now carries the unresolved shadow of Mr. L, Guild contracts, haunted technology, medical testimony, and a disappearance mystery too large to fit inside the word sidekick. Waluigi finds Luigi infuriating, sympathetic, suspicious, brave, evasive, and extremely bad at choosing restful employment. The Poltergust is not just a vacuum; it is Luigi’s proof that fear can be weaponized into duty. The Garden Above the Fire confirms that Luigi survived the lava-falls aftermath, recalled the line 'The star is not lost. Find the garden above the fire,' and reached Dr. Toad's clinic alive — still wounded, still asking for Mario, but no longer missing in the compound tunnels.
description:
Waluigi finds writing this entry physically painful, but historical accuracy demands it. Luigi has spent most public history being treated as an appendix to Mario. That is lazy history. Waluigi enjoys insulting Luigi personally, but Waluigi refuses to let history insult him inaccurately.

## The Brother Problem

Luigi’s public identity was built in relation to Mario, which is unfair and historically dangerous. A person defined as the second brother can disappear in plain sight because institutions file him under support, not center. This is why Luigi’s records are uneven: sports appearances, ghost incidents, heroic support, then sudden gaps, Mr. L references, Guild contracts, and medical testimony. The shape of the record tells Waluigi that Luigi mattered more than the public was encouraged to understand. Mario is the heroic sun of the old Mushroom myth. Luigi is not simply the moon. He is the eclipse nobody wrote procedures for.

## Fear as Method

Luigi is afraid often. This is not a weakness in the usual sense; it is his operating environment. Many fighters rely on anger, duty, pride, or confidence. Luigi relies on fear processed into procedure. He shakes, complains, startles, and then points the Poltergust at the ghost anyway. Haunted places punish arrogance. Luigi’s fear makes him observant. He notices the wrong temperature, the hallway that feels longer on the way back, the portrait watching too calmly. Fear keeps the instrument panel lit. Waluigi hates how useful that is.

## The Poltergust

The Poltergust is not just a vacuum. It is a technological interface between living fear and dead persistence. Professor E. Gadd’s paratechnology turns Luigi’s terror into steps: strobe, suction, containment, breathe, scream, continue. The device can capture spectral entities, disrupt supernatural threats, and carry ghosts no sane person would want on their back. This is why Waluigi classifies Poltergust use as Technique, not Arcane. Luigi is not casting spells every time the room is haunted. He is operating specialized equipment under pressure, which is more impressive and more embarrassing for everyone who laughed at him.

## Mr. L

The Mr. L problem cannot be avoided. The official narrative says Luigi was corrupted into an alternate persona: confident where Luigi was anxious, aggressive where Luigi was hesitant, cruel where Luigi was compassionate. Waluigi does not fully trust a story that clean. It absolves the kingdom, isolates the blame in outside corruption, and lets everyone pretend the matter ended when Mario won. But Mr. L revealed capacities the public Luigi hid: piloting, engineering confidence, theatrical aggression, and the ability to stand against Mario. Whether these came from corruption alone or from something Luigi already carried, the record remains dangerous.

## The Ruined Manor Contract

Luigi arrived at the Ruined Manor under Guild contract. That should concern everyone because the Mages’ Guild does not hire people out of kindness; it identifies capabilities and assigns uses. Luigi’s job was to remove spectral anomalies with the Poltergust. The phrasing sounds simple until one remembers the manor was tied to dimensional fractures, aristocratic secrets, Archie Miser’s fire problems, Bones’s infiltration, and Guild containment logic. Luigi performed useful work: stunning ghosts, vacuuming threats, opening doors, and containing things he refused to discuss later. Waluigi dislikes admitting this, so Waluigi will say it once: Luigi was competent.

## The Bubble Bath Incident

While others were engaged in danger and espionage, Luigi took a luxurious bubble bath, claiming it helped expel ectoplasm. Waluigi remains offended. Waluigi also now understands that this may have been self-care, decontamination, avoidance, or the nervous system demanding one room where fear did not get to drive. The bath is ridiculous. It is also revealing. Luigi copes through rituals: clean the body, reset the breath, pretend the warm water makes the room safe. Waluigi reserves the right to mock him and the responsibility to file the coping mechanism accurately.

## The Waiting Room Testimony

The Waiting Room testimony makes Luigi’s file much darker. It suggests medical intervention, containment protocols, possible Dr. Mario or Uncle Dario identity confusion, and a set of circumstances that threaten several assumptions about the Mario Brothers. In that testimony, Luigi is not the ghostbuster. He is the body being managed by systems larger than him. If even half of that account is true, Luigi has been handled, moved, treated, and remembered through channels the public heroic narrative does not admit. Waluigi does not yet know the whole truth. Waluigi knows the gaps are shaped like people hiding something.

## Relationship to the Mages Guild

Luigi’s relationship with the Mages’ Guild is useful and dangerous. Individual Guild operatives may respect him. The institution still sees a man with ghost technology as an asset. The Guild loves assets. It loves contracts, badges, containment, tracking, and the kind of consent that becomes complicated when the alternative is being left alone with the haunted problem. Every Guild-Luigi interaction should be read with one question: did Luigi choose this, or was the task placed where his conscience would have to pick it up?

## Relationship to Disaster Inc.

Luigi is not a core member of Disaster Inc., but his path crosses theirs in ways that matter. He intersects with Archie, Bones, Bowser, Agent L, ruined manor incidents, ghost technology, and the Mario mystery. His relationship with Archie is especially strange: fire and fear, improvisation and procedure, guilt and anxiety. They should not work well together. Sometimes they do because both understand what it means to be used by stories larger than themselves. Bowser complicates things further because Bowser may have been falsely blamed for Peach’s death. Luigi’s old heroic framework no longer fits cleanly. Waluigi suspects Luigi knows this and hates it.

## Waluigi Assessment

Luigi is annoying, brave, evasive, useful, wounded, and much more important than the word sidekick allows. The Poltergust makes him dangerous to ghosts. Mr. L makes him dangerous to simple narratives. The Waiting Room makes him dangerous to official records. His fear makes him human. His persistence makes him heroic in the least convenient way for Waluigi’s ego. Waluigi will continue investigating Luigi because the green plumber’s file touches too many locked doors. Waluigi will also continue mocking Luigi because truth without style is just paperwork. WAH.

## The Garden Above the Fire

The lava-bridge file no longer ends with Luigi lost past the falls. Waluigi's crew found him alive in the volcanic tunnel system, burned across the arms and legs, delirious from pain and exhaustion, and still able to remember the courier note's line: *the star is not lost; find the garden above the fire*. Dr. Toad's chart makes the medical fact plain — serious but treatable burns, rest required, no adventuring — while the emotional fact is less tidy: Luigi asked whether he and Mario were still superstars, and Waluigi answered because Mario was not there to do it.

**Backfilled from 2 Aethel, 1035 BF.** On the night the rest order expired, Wario's paid informant upgraded the lockdown report to a private wing, high security, and 'consciousness fluxing' — three phrases written down in a moving aircraft that nobody has verified. The helicopter sent to check crashed on the storehouse roof next door; the pair reached the street and a stairwell and never saw a patient. What they did see, outside the clinic, was Mr. L — in Luigi's clothes, in the open, in three copies. Whether Luigi is upstairs, and what was standing outside his window if he is, are the two open questions the archive carried off Star Hill on foot.

faiths.note: Luigi keeps the observances he was raised with, which in his case means sketching the North Star on waking in houses that are not haunted, and doing it faster in houses that are.

Whatever E. Gadd's Method is, Luigi is its most experienced field practitioner and its least willing one. He has operated the Poltergust in conditions the Method's own literature calls theoretical. The contract is with the Guild now, which has not improved the working relationship with the doctrine.

name: Chief Thornpaw
title: The Rakasha Who Loved a Princess
status: Active — still leading his people after eighty-five years, which raises questions about Rakasha lifespans
summary: Chief Thornpaw is the leader of the Rakasha and—according to his own testimony at Fawful's gala—was involved in a secret relationship with Princess Peach before her assassination. He claims to have been shown the secret hatch in her chambers, to have visited her privately through that passage, and to have fathered a child with her. If his testimony is accurate, he is one of the most important witnesses to the events surrounding the assassination. If his testimony is fabricated or manipulated, he may be something else entirely—a plant, a patsy, or a participant in whatever actually happened. Waluigi has learned to be careful about accepting testimony at face value, even testimony that seems emotionally authentic. Especially testimony that seems emotionally authentic. Grief can be performed. Love can be invented. And Thornpaw has had eighty-five years to construct whatever narrative serves his purposes. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is going to document Chief Thornpaw carefully, because Thornpaw occupies an unusual position in Waluigi's investigation: he is simultaneously the most SYMPATHETIC figure connected to the assassination and the most SUSPICIOUS.

Sympathetic because his account—of forbidden love, devastating loss, decades of silent grief—is emotionally compelling. Waluigi is not immune to emotional compelling. Waluigi has FEELINGS, even if Waluigi expresses them primarily through athletic competition and justified grievance.

Suspicious because Thornpaw's testimony provides EXACTLY what the Loyalist narrative needed: confirmation of the secret relationship, the secret hatch, the secret heir. His revelation at Fawful's gala came at a politically convenient moment, supported claims that were otherwise unverifiable, and transformed him from a minor regional leader into a central figure in the assassination mystery.

Convenient testimony is not necessarily FALSE testimony. But Waluigi notes the convenience.

## Who Are the Rakasha?

Before examining Thornpaw specifically, Waluigi must establish context about his people.

The Rakasha are a culture indigenous to territories east and south of the Mushroom Kingdom. They are sometimes described as 'lion-like' or 'feline,' though Waluigi has seen enough Rakasha to know that this description oversimplifies significant physical variation among them. Some are indeed feline in appearance. Others are more humanoid. Still others have characteristics Waluigi cannot easily categorize.

Rakasha society is organized around tribal structures led by chiefs who earn their positions through demonstrated wisdom and strength rather than hereditary succession. This makes Thornpaw's eighty-five-year tenure as chief notable—he has apparently maintained his people's confidence across nearly a century.

Rakasha spiritual traditions include 'spirit-walkers'—individuals who can traverse dimensional boundaries and communicate across planar divides. This capability becomes increasingly relevant given the Planar Fracture and current dimensional instability. Ryan—a member of Disaster Inc.—was taken in by a Rakasha spirit-walker after jumping from the Vigilance, suggesting ongoing Rakasha involvement in current events.

The Mushroom Kingdom's historical relationship with the Rakasha has been complicated. The court conservatives—the same factions Loyalists accuse of enabling Peach's assassination—regarded the Rakasha with suspicion. Inter-marriage between nobles and Rakasha was forbidden by social custom if not explicit law. A ROYAL relationship with a Rakasha would have been politically explosive.

This context makes Thornpaw's claimed relationship with Peach either remarkably brave or remarkably dangerous—depending on perspective.

## The Relationship Claim — What Thornpaw Says

At Fawful's gala in 1040 BF, Chief Thornpaw spoke with Mistveil—a Loyalist intelligence operative. According to reports Waluigi has obtained (secondhand, so appropriate skepticism applies), Thornpaw confirmed:

1. He and Princess Peach were involved in a romantic relationship.
2. The relationship was secret, known only to a small circle.
3. Peach showed him the secret hatch—a hidden passage in her chambers.
4. He used this passage to visit her privately.
5. Their relationship produced a child—a half-Human, half-Rakasha heir.
6. He believes the conspiracy against Peach was motivated partly by preventing this child from taking the throne.

This testimony aligns PERFECTLY with the Loyalist narrative about the assassination. Too perfectly, perhaps. Or perhaps the Loyalist narrative has been accurate all along and Thornpaw's confirmation simply validates what investigators like Captain Toadette have believed for decades.

Waluigi cannot determine which interpretation is correct.

## Supporting Evidence — What Corroborates Thornpaw's Claims?

**Lady Bloomia's Testimony:**

If Bloomia's account in 'Coronation Day' is authentic, she overheard conversations between Peach and an unidentified male visitor on the morning of the assassination. She describes 'the sound of something I will not describe, because it was not meant for my ears.' She noticed the smell of 'earth and pine' in the Princess's chambers—which could be consistent with a Rakasha visitor.

However, Bloomia's testimony does not NAME Thornpaw. It describes a male visitor with a 'deep, rough' voice and an unidentified accent. This could be Thornpaw. It could also be someone else.

**The Secret Hatch:**

The hatch's existence seems to be confirmed by multiple sources—Bloomia's account, Thornpaw's testimony, and Loyalist investigators who claim to have found physical evidence of the passage during their archival research. If the hatch existed, SOMEONE was using it. Thornpaw claims it was him.

**The Child:**

No independent evidence of the child has been presented. If the child exists, they would be approximately eighty-five years old now. Their location, identity, and status are unknown. The Loyalists believe the child survived (possibly smuggled out by Bloomia). Others suggest the child may never have existed—a detail fabricated to provide motive for the conspiracy.

## Contradicting Evidence — What Undermines Thornpaw's Claims?

**Timing of Revelation:**

Thornpaw remained silent for EIGHTY-FIVE YEARS about his relationship with Peach. He revealed it in 1040 BF—exactly when the Loyalists needed confirmation for their narrative, exactly when the Regency was weakening, exactly when maximum political impact could be achieved.

Why now? Thornpaw might answer that he was protecting his people, his child, or himself. Speaking earlier would have invited Regency or Guild retaliation. Speaking now, with the old order crumbling, carries less risk.

But Waluigi notes that convenient timing can indicate coordinated strategy as easily as genuine revelation.

**No Corroborating Witnesses:**

Thornpaw claims the relationship was secret and known only to a small circle. But NONE of that circle has come forward. No Rakasha elder confirming they knew. No palace servant who noticed signs of the affair. No member of Peach's inner circle verifying the story.

The relationship—if real—was apparently perfectly concealed for decades before the assassination and perfectly concealed for eighty-five years after. This level of secrecy is possible but remarkable.

**Thornpaw's Position:**

Thornpaw is the chief of a people who have been marginalized by the Mushroom Kingdom for generations. The civil war created by Peach's assassination has weakened the kingdom that marginalized them. The Loyalists—who now seek Thornpaw's testimony—oppose the Regency that opposed Rakasha integration.

Thornpaw has MOTIVE to support the Loyalist narrative regardless of whether it's true. Supporting the enemies of your enemies is basic politics. If his testimony helps destroy the Regency, his people benefit—whether or not the testimony is accurate.

## The Uncomfortable Possibility — Could Thornpaw Be Involved?

Waluigi must address a theory that most commentators avoid: Thornpaw as participant rather than witness.

**Access:**

Thornpaw—by his own admission—knew about the secret hatch and used it to enter Peach's chambers. He had access that bypassed all security. If he shared this information with others—or if he himself was the killer—the assassination becomes logistically simpler.

**Motive:**

If the relationship soured, Thornpaw might have had reason to act against Peach. If she threatened to disinherit the child, or end the relationship, or take some other action that Thornpaw opposed, he had both access and motive.

Alternatively, Thornpaw might have been COERCED. Someone learned about the secret relationship and threatened to expose it unless Thornpaw cooperated. He provided the hatch information under duress. The assassination was his fault—not through malice but through weakness.

**The Grief Performance:**

Thornpaw's apparent grief at Fawful's gala is cited as evidence of his innocence. But grief can be performed. Eighty-five years is enough time to construct any emotional presentation you want. If Thornpaw is guilty—of direct involvement or of providing information under pressure—performing grief would be essential to maintaining his position.

Waluigi does NOT accuse Thornpaw. Waluigi has no evidence of his guilt. But Waluigi notes that his ACCESS makes him a logical suspect, and his TESTIMONY makes him a logical witness, and these roles are not easily distinguished from outside.

## The Spirit-Walker Connection

Thornpaw leads a people with dimensional capabilities. Rakasha spirit-walkers can traverse planar boundaries. This becomes relevant in the current crisis.

Ryan of Disaster Inc. was taken in by a Rakasha spirit-walker after jumping from the Vigilance. This spirit-walker presumably reports to Thornpaw or operates within Thornpaw's sphere of influence. If so, Thornpaw has current intelligence about Disaster Inc.'s activities.

The Planar Fracture has created dimensional instability that spirit-walker capabilities might help address—or exploit. The Rakasha are one of the few factions with existing dimensional expertise. This makes them valuable allies to whoever seeks to resolve the crisis... or valuable assets to whoever seeks to deepen it.

Thornpaw's revelation at Fawful's gala might have been motivated by more than desire for justice. It might have been positioning—establishing himself as a central figure in events that are about to become even more significant.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Chief Thornpaw is either:

1. A tragic figure who loved a princess, lost her to conspiracy, and has finally found the courage to speak after eighty-five years of silence.

2. A calculating leader who invented or exaggerated a relationship to position himself advantageously in the current political chaos.

3. A guilty party using testimony to deflect suspicion from his own involvement.

4. A coerced witness whose original cooperation enabled the assassination and whose current testimony is an attempt at redemption.

5. Some combination of the above.

Waluigi cannot determine which. The emotional authenticity of Thornpaw's grief SEEMS genuine, but Waluigi has been fooled by emotional authenticity before. Waluigi's rivals often seem genuinely upset when Waluigi beats them at tennis. Doesn't mean they're telling the truth about the net height being regulation.

What Waluigi believes:

- Thornpaw knows MORE than he has revealed. Whether this additional knowledge incriminates others or himself, Waluigi cannot say.
- The timing of his revelation is politically significant. Whatever motivated it, the effect serves Loyalist interests.
- The child—if the child exists—is one of the most important figures in the Mushroom Kingdom, and Thornpaw presumably knows their location.
- Thornpaw's people are positioned to play a significant role in the current crisis. Their dimensional capabilities make them valuable to all factions.

Waluigi will continue investigating. Thornpaw is either a key witness or a key suspect, and possibly both. Either way, understanding him is essential to understanding what actually happened eighty-five years ago.

WAH.

faiths.note: The Rakasha kept dimensional traditions centuries before the Mages' Guild existed, and the Pact's reverence for the trees that connect realms is the closest published doctrine to what Thornpaw's shamans actually practise. He also testified at Fawful's gala to a secret relationship with Princess Peach, which no tradition covers.

name: Captain Toadette
title: The Ruthless Restorer
status: Active — back from Warp Pipe Junction with dull claws and a closed question about rats
summary: Captain Toadette is the military commander of the Peach Loyalists and the scariest person in the Mushroom Kingdom who isn't a dimensional horror or a kaiju. She plans operations with tactical brilliance, executes them with total commitment, and maintains a no-prisoners policy that would make the Iron Legion uncomfortable. Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser and felt LESS uneasy than he does contemplating Captain Toadette.
description:
Waluigi has met Toadette before the current crisis, in the context of sports events and party games. She was competitive, capable, and had excellent sportsmanship. The Toadette who commands the Peach Loyalists is... different. Something happened—the death of Princess Peach, the circumstances surrounding it, the feeling of being unable to prevent a catastrophe that should have been preventable—and the result is a military commander who has replaced sportsmanship with zealotry.

## Military Capabilities

Toadette is a BRILLIANT tactician. This is not an exaggeration or a concession—it's a statement of fact that makes everything else about her more dangerous. The Fall of Bramblehaven was a masterpiece of siege warfare: sappers tunneling overnight, three simultaneous breach attacks, coordinated assault teams that took a fortified bastion in a single day. That level of planning requires intelligence, patience, and strategic vision.

She also shot one of her own sergeants for suggesting a tactical retreat.

This combination—tactical brilliance plus absolute moral certainty—is what makes Toadette terrifying. She's not cruel for the sake of cruelty. She genuinely believes that Princess Peach's cause demands total commitment, and total commitment means NO compromise. No retreats. No prisoners. Everything sacrificed on the altar of a dead princess's memory.

## The No-Quarter Policy

After Bramblehaven fell, fifteen garrison troops attempted to surrender. They put down their weapons, raised their hands, and gave up. Toadette's standing orders were clear: no prisoners from Fawful's forces. The surrendering troops were executed in the keep's courtyard.

Some individual Loyalist soldiers reportedly hesitated or refused. They were overruled. The executions proceeded. By nightfall, Bramblehaven was silent.

Waluigi has done questionable things in his life. He's cheated at tennis. He's participated in schemes with Wario that skirted the boundaries of law and good taste. But there are LINES, and executing surrendering enemies is so far past the line that the line is a dot on the horizon. Toadette crosses that line as a matter of policy. Deliberately. Repeatedly.

## The Peach Connection

What makes Toadette tragic—and Waluigi uses that word deliberately—is that she's doing all of this for Princess Peach, and Waluigi knew Peach. Waluigi COMPETED against Peach. Princess Peach was kind, gracious, and had the kind of sportsmanship that made losing to her slightly less infuriating than it should have been.

Peach would not have approved of what is being done in her name. Waluigi is absolutely certain of this. Princess Peach would not have ordered prisoners executed. She would not have shot her own soldiers for suggesting retreat. She would not have demanded the kind of total war that Toadette wages.

But Peach is dead, and the Loyalists aren't asking her opinion. They're asking her MEMORY, and memory doesn't talk back. Toadette is fighting for a Princess Peach who exists only in her own grief—a version of Peach who would approve of atrocities, who would demand blood for blood, who would see total war as justice. This version never existed. But Toadette has built a military movement on serving it.

## Assessment

Waluigi fears Captain Toadette in a way he fears very few people. General Ironhand is terrifying because he's indifferent—he'll kill you and feel nothing. Toadette is terrifying because she BELIEVES—she'll kill you and feel righteous. The Iron Legion is a machine. The Peach Loyalists are a crusade.

Machines can be broken. Crusades are harder to stop.

Waluigi hopes Toadette finds something—a piece of evidence, a surviving memory, a ghost of the real Peach telling her to STOP—that brings her back from the edge she's standing on. But Waluigi also knows that people who have committed atrocities often can't turn back because turning back would mean confronting what they've done. It's easier to keep going, to add more sins to the pile, to believe that eventual victory will justify everything.

Waluigi does not think victory justifies everything. Waluigi thinks some things CANNOT be justified, only done or not done. Toadette has chosen to do them.

WAH.

faiths.note: Toadette prays before operations and considers this a logistical step rather than a spiritual one. The Loyalists fight for a dead Princess; the faith supplies the vocabulary that makes eighty-five years of that sound like duty instead of grief.
The chivalric code arrived with a captured Chramalot manual and Toadette kept the parts about honouring surrender. Her officers report that she means them, which is the inconvenient part.
